Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the producer licence renewal and CE calendar for every jurisdiction the group distributes in; escalates lapse risk to the Producer Compliance Manager

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - IAIS ICP 18 (Intermediaries), Standards 18.1-18.3 (licensing and ongoing competence of intermediaries) read together with each host-jurisdiction renewal rule (US state licence renewal statutes and CE regulations, Canadian provincial AIC renewal rules, UK FCA TC 2.1 competence); re-read at each renewal cycle open

In-scope processes.value: Producer licence renewal and continuing-education tracking for all appointed and contracted producers and licensed employees, from renewal-window open through renewal confirmation and CE transcript posting

In-scope systems.value: NIPR Gateway PDB licence/CE data feeding the agency/producer management system; CE completions posted from the learning management system

Compliance procedure documented.value: Producer Licence Renewal & CE Procedure - renewal-window extract, CE credit-gap calculation, producer notification at 120/90/60/30 days, renewal submission, lapse suspension of appointments and commissions

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Producer Compliance Manager and Head of Compliance; refreshed each January and on any state CE rule change or NIPR Gateway release note

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per-producer renewal due date (US resident licences on birth-month or biennial anniversary cycles, non-resident on the resident cycle) with CE credits completed before the licence expiry date - typically 24 credits including 3 ethics per two-year cycle, plus the 4-credit NAIC annuity best-interest training before any annuity sale

Deadline reminders configured.value: Automated producer emails at T-120, T-90, T-60, T-30 and T-7 days to licence expiry, plus a weekly Licensing Ops worklist of producers with a CE credit gap inside 60 days

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Renewal log, NIPR renewal confirmations and transaction IDs, CE transcripts and course completion certificates retained 7 years from licence termination in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any lapsed licence, missed CE deadline or post-expiry solicitation is logged as a licensing exception with lapse dates, business written while unlicensed and reinstatement disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every lapse remediation, reinstatement and any commission held or clawed back for business written on an expired licence

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All producer licences with an expiry date inside the tested renewal cycle, per the NIPR PDB roster reconciled to active contracts in the agency/producer management system

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance for business solicited on an expired licence; renewal-on-time rate must be 100% for appointed producers, and any CE deficiency uncured at expiry is a fail regardless of later reinstatement

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation runs on a continuous renewal cycle; test executes quarterly over the licences expiring in that quarter plus 100% of the prior quarter's lapse exceptions

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have submitted any sampled renewal, assigned any CE course or dispositioned any lapse being tested

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly Producer Licence & CE test workpaper (PDB extract, roster reconciliation, sample, re-performance screenshots, exception schedule) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Renewal log export with NIPR transaction IDs, CE transcripts and lapse remediation notes, producible for a market conduct exam licensing standard request within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Producer Compliance Manager answers state DOI licensing inquiries; Regulatory Counsel clears any self-report of business written by an unlicensed or lapsed producer before it leaves the building

checklist.step: Open the renewal cycle and extract every licence expiring in the window
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Reports > Producer Database (PDB) Reports and run the firm's bulk PDB report by NPN list for all resident and non-resident licences.

Filter the extract to licences with an expiry date in the next 150 days and export to the renewal log with columns NPN, producer name, state, licence class, lines of authority, expiry date, resident/non-resident flag.
Ask Distribution Operations for the list of producers under an active contract so terminated producers are dropped from the renewal spend.
Save the dated extract as renewal-cycle-<yyyy-qq>-pdb.csv in the compliance evidence repository as the cycle baseline.
checklist.done: the renewal log holds one row per expiring licence with NPN, state, class, lines of authority and expiry date, restricted to contracted producers.

checklist.step: Confirm each jurisdiction's current renewal rule and fee
actions: For every state in the log open the NIPR State Licensing Requirements page and read the renewal cycle basis (birth month, anniversary, fixed biennial date), the renewal fee, the late/reinstatement window and whether renewal is electronic through NIPR or state-portal only.

For Canadian producers open the provincial regulator's licensing page (e.g. AIC Alberta, FSRA Ontario) and record the renewal date and CE hours; for UK-appointed representatives record the FCA TC competence attestation date.
Write the rule basis, fee and reinstatement window onto each renewal-log row.
Print each state requirements page to PDF named <state>-renewal-rules-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf as the evidence behind the due-date calculation.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction on the log carries a cycle basis, fee, reinstatement window and a dated rules capture.

checklist.step: Pull each producer's CE transcript and compute the credit gap
actions: In NIPR Gateway open the PDB CE Compliance view for each NPN and read credits earned, ethics credits earned and the CE compliance status for the current cycle.
Pull internal course completions from the learning management system transcript report for the same producers and match them to state-approved course numbers.

Compute per producer: credits required minus credits banked, split into general credits, ethics credits, annuity best-interest (NAIC Model 275, 4 credits) and any long-term-care or flood-specific requirement.
Write the gap onto the renewal-log row and flag any producer whose gap exceeds the credits obtainable inside the remaining window.
checklist.done: each producer row shows credits required, credits banked, the split by credit type and a computed gap.

checklist.step: Assign the courses that actually close the gap
actions: Take the gap list from Licensing Ops and, for each producer, select courses whose state-approved provider and course numbers are valid in that producer's resident state.
Enrol the producer in the LMS curriculum, setting the due date 30 days before the licence expiry date so credits can be reported to the state in time.
Enrol every producer selling annuities in the 4-credit best-interest course and, where the state requires it, the product-specific carrier training before appointment activation.
Return the enrolment confirmation report to the Producer Licensing Coordinator for posting onto the renewal log.
checklist.done: every producer with a gap has state-valid courses assigned and due at least 30 days before licence expiry.

checklist.step: Notify producers on the escalation schedule and record acknowledgement
actions: Trigger the templated renewal notice at T-120, T-90, T-60, T-30 and T-7 days, listing the producer's expiry date, outstanding CE credits, the renewal fee and who pays it.
Route T-30 and T-7 notices to the producer's Agency Relations Manager as well, so the distribution relationship owner is chasing alongside Licensing Ops.
Record the send date and any producer reply on the renewal-log row; unresponsive producers at T-30 go onto the weekly lapse-risk call agenda.
For agency-billed licences confirm with the agency principal in writing who is submitting the renewal.
checklist.done: every expiring licence has a dated notification trail through T-7 and a named chaser for anything unanswered.

checklist.step: Verify CE credits have posted to the state before submitting the renewal
actions: Re-run the PDB CE Compliance view 15 days before each expiry and confirm the state CE transcript shows status Compliant, not merely the internal LMS completion.
Where the LMS shows a completion the state does not, contact the course provider (Prometric, Pearson VUE or the approved vendor) to have the roster re-transmitted and log the ticket reference.
Hold the renewal submission for any producer whose state CE status is still deficient - a renewal filed against a deficient transcript will reject and burn the fee.
Update the renewal-log row with the CE-verified date and the source screen capture.
checklist.done: no renewal is submitted until the state's own CE record reads compliant for that producer and cycle.

checklist.step: Submit the renewal transaction and capture the confirmation
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Licensing > License Renewal, select the state and enter the NPN batch for that state's renewal window.
Review the renewal application answers, in particular the background/regulatory-action questions, against the producer's current attestation before authorising submission.
Pay the state renewal fee plus the NIPR transaction fee from the licensing funding account and submit.
Download the NIPR transaction confirmation and record the transaction ID, submission date, fee paid and new expiry date on the renewal-log row.
checklist.done: each renewal has a NIPR transaction ID, a paid fee, and a new expiry date written to the renewal log.

checklist.step: Confirm the state actually issued the renewed licence
actions: Five business days after submission re-query the PDB for each NPN and read Licence Status and Expiry Date.
Treat anything other than Active with a forward expiry date as unresolved - open the state's own licensee lookup and, where needed, email the state DOI licensing desk quoting the NIPR transaction ID.
Attach the refreshed PDB record to the renewal-log row as proof of issuance.
Escalate any state that has not issued within 15 days to the Producer Compliance Manager for direct DOI follow-up.
checklist.done: every submitted renewal is confirmed Active in the PDB with a forward expiry date, or is under a logged DOI follow-up.

checklist.step: Push the refreshed licence data into the downstream systems
actions: Load the renewed licence status, expiry date and lines of authority into the producer master record so the writing-eligibility flag recalculates.
Confirm the nightly feed reached the policy administration and new-business systems so an expired producer cannot be selected as writing agent on a new application.
Reconcile the record count loaded against the count submitted and investigate any difference the same day.
Notify Commission Operations of any producer whose eligibility flag flipped so commission processing follows the licence.
checklist.done: producer master, new-business eligibility and commission systems all reflect the renewed expiry dates with a reconciled record count.

checklist.step: Suspend writing authority and commissions the moment a licence lapses
actions: Run the daily expired-licence exception report and set the producer's status to Suspended - Licence Lapsed on the day after expiry.
Instruct Commission Operations to place new commissions in a hold suspense account rather than paying them while the licence is lapsed.
Ask New Business for any application dated on or after the expiry date with that producer as writing agent and quantify premium written while unlicensed.
Open a licensing exception record capturing lapse date, business written, states affected and the reinstatement plan.
checklist.done: every lapsed producer is suspended on day one, commissions are held, and business written post-expiry is quantified.

checklist.step: Reinstate lapsed licences through the state's own reinstatement path
actions: Read the state's reinstatement rule (commonly a 12-month window with a late penalty, after which the producer must re-examine) and record which path applies.
Where reinstatement is available, complete the outstanding CE first, then submit the reinstatement in NIPR Gateway with the late fee.
Where the window has closed, hand the producer to Licensing Ops onboarding for full re-application including pre-licensing education and examination.
Record the reinstatement or re-application route, cost and completion date on the exception record.
checklist.done: each lapsed licence is either reinstated with a dated confirmation or moved onto a documented re-application path.

checklist.step: Decide the treatment of business written while the licence was lapsed
actions: Review the quantified post-expiry business against the state's unlicensed-activity statute and any commission-sharing prohibition.
Decide per state whether commissions must be forfeited or redirected to a licensed agent of record, and whether a self-report to the DOI is required.
Draft any self-report letter and record the DOI reference number and response.
Write the decision, rationale and citation onto the licensing exception record and release or claw back the held commissions accordingly.
checklist.done: every post-expiry sale has a written counsel decision on commissions and self-reporting, with a citation.

checklist.step: Report renewal and CE status to the distribution governance forum
actions: Build the cycle dashboard: licences due, renewed on time, renewed late, lapsed, CE-deficient at T-30, and premium written while lapsed.
Trend the on-time renewal rate against the prior four quarters and call out any agency or state driving the misses.
Present the pack to the Distribution Compliance forum with named owners and dates for each remediation.
File the pack and the minutes in the compliance evidence repository as ICP 18 supervisory evidence.
checklist.done: a dated governance pack shows on-time renewal rate, lapse count, CE deficiencies and owned remediations.

checklist.step: Refresh the calendar rules whenever a jurisdiction changes its requirement
actions: Subscribe to state DOI bulletins and NIPR release notes, and review new items weekly for changes to renewal cycles, CE hours, ethics splits or annuity training requirements.
Where a rule changes, update the jurisdiction rule table in the licensing system and re-run the credit-gap calculation for affected producers.
Notify Learning & Development so the course catalogue is re-mapped before the next cycle opens.
Log the change, effective date and source citation in the regulatory change record.
checklist.done: the jurisdiction rule table matches current bulletins and every change has a logged source and effective date.

checklist.step: File the cycle evidence under retention
actions: Move the renewal log, PDB extracts, NIPR confirmations, CE transcripts and exception records into the repository under renewal cycle and jurisdiction.
Apply the 7-years-from-licence-termination retention label so records survive producer departure.
Confirm the index makes records retrievable by NPN, state and expiry date for exam response.
Run the completeness check that every renewal-log row has an attached confirmation before closing the cycle.
checklist.done: the cycle record set is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by NPN and state with no unattached rows.

testing.step: Build the population of licences that expired in the tested period
actions: Run an independent bulk PDB report over the firm's full NPN list and select every licence with an expiry date inside the quarter.
Add licences terminated mid-quarter so producers who left before renewing cannot fall out of scope.
Reconcile the count to the Licensing Ops renewal log and investigate every difference before sampling.
Sign the population as complete, recording the extract date and record count.
testing.done: the population is independently extracted, reconciled to the renewal log, and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the roster used for the cycle to active producer contracts
actions: Extract all producers with an active contract and at least one appointment during the quarter.
Match to the PDB population on NPN and list producers with an active contract but no licence row - these are the highest-risk misses.
List producers licensed but never loaded to the licensing calendar and trace how they were missed.
Record both difference lists as candidate exceptions in the workpaper.
testing.done: contracted-producer and licensed-producer populations are reconciled, with both unmatched lists documented.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of lapses, late renewals and reinstatements in the quarter.
Take 30 renewals at random (seeded, reproducible) across at least eight states, including two non-US jurisdictions where the group is licensed.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and stratification in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
Confirm the sample includes at least five annuity-selling producers so the best-interest training requirement is exercised.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all lapses plus 30 random renewals and annuity producers is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the licence status check in the regulator's own record
actions: For each sampled NPN query the PDB directly and read Licence Status, class, lines of authority and expiry date without first reading the renewal log.
Compare your reading to the renewal-log row; any difference in status, expiry date or lines of authority is an exception.
Where the PDB and the state's own licensee lookup disagree, treat the state record as authoritative and note the discrepancy.
Capture the PDB record screen into the workpaper for each sampled producer.
testing.done: each sampled licence has an independent PDB reading captured and compared to the renewal log.

testing.step: Re-perform the CE credit calculation against the state transcript
actions: For each sampled producer read the state CE transcript and total general credits, ethics credits and any product-specific credits earned in the cycle.
Compare to that state's published requirement (for example 24 credits including 3 ethics per biennium) and recompute compliant/deficient yourself.
Confirm the annuity best-interest 4-credit course was completed before the producer's first annuity sale date, not merely before renewal.
Log as an exception any producer renewed while the state transcript read deficient, and any credit counted twice across cycles.
testing.done: CE compliance is independently recomputed per sampled producer and every credit shortfall or double-count is logged.

testing.step: Trace each sampled renewal to its NIPR transaction and fee
actions: Search the recorded NIPR transaction ID and confirm it belongs to the sampled NPN, state and licence class.
Compare the submission date to the expiry date and mark any renewal filed after expiry as late.
Agree the fee paid to the state's published renewal fee and the licensing funding account statement.
Attach the transaction confirmation to the workpaper for each sampled row.
testing.done: every sampled renewal traces to a genuine NIPR transaction with an agreed fee and a dated submission.

testing.step: Recompute the notification schedule and the lapse-day suspension
actions: Recompute the T-120/T-90/T-60/T-30/T-7 notice dates from each sampled expiry date and compare to the actual send dates in the notification log.
For each lapse, confirm the producer status changed to Suspended - Licence Lapsed no later than the first day after expiry.
Confirm commissions were placed in suspense from the same date and not paid during the lapse.
Treat any notice never sent, or any suspension applied more than one day late, as an exception.
testing.done: notice dates and suspension timing are recomputed against expiry dates and every lag is quantified.

testing.step: Test whether any business was solicited on an expired licence
actions: Extract all new-business applications in the quarter with application date, state and writing-agent NPN.
Join to the PDB licence history and flag every application whose date falls outside the writing agent's licensed period in that state.
Quantify premium and commission on each flagged application and confirm each one appears on the licensing exception record.
Escalate any flagged application not already known to Licensing Ops as a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: unlicensed-activity applications are identified by system join, quantified, and matched to logged exceptions.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception recording NPN, state, expiry date, what failed and the customer or commission impact.
Assign a root cause (producer non-response, CE not transmitted by provider, stale jurisdiction rule, roster gap) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, for unlicensed activity, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception carries an issue reference, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-time renewal rate, the CE-deficient-at-expiry count and premium written while lapsed, and compare to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have a reviewer who performed none of the renewals sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any unlicensed-activity breach to the Distribution Compliance forum at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the on-time rate, exception count, conclusion and the governance reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the fitness-and-propriety screen for every new hire, producer and agency principal, including the 18 U.S.C. 1033 prohibited-person determination and written-consent path

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - IAIS ICP 5 (Suitability of Persons), Standards 5.2-5.5 and ICP 18 (Intermediaries) on fit-and-proper intermediaries, applied through 18 U.S.C. 1033/1034 (felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust) and each state's 1033 written-consent procedure; also FCA FIT 1-2 for UK-regulated staff and OSFI B-20 style fitness checks for Canadian entities

In-scope processes.value: Pre-hire screening for all employees engaged in the business of insurance and pre-contract screening for producers, agencies and agency principals, plus event-driven re-screening on any reported criminal charge or regulatory action

In-scope systems.value: Criminal, sanctions and regulatory-action screening in LexisNexis Risk with fingerprint results from the state-designated vendor, results attached to the candidate record in the HRIS and to the producer record in the agency/producer management system

Compliance procedure documented.value: Fitness & Propriety Screening Procedure - consent capture, background package scope, PDB regulatory-action review, 1033 disposition matrix, adverse-action process under FCRA, and 1033 written-consent application

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with Employment Counsel concurrence on the adverse-action and ban-the-box steps; reviewed annually and on any state 1033 consent-procedure change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per candidate - screening cleared before the start date or contract effective date; FCRA pre-adverse-action notice with a minimum 5 business-day dispute window before final adverse action; producer regulatory-action disclosures reported to the state within 30 days of the final order

Deadline reminders configured.value: Recruiting workflow alerts when a screening is open more than 7 days, when a start date falls inside 5 days with the screen unresolved, and at day 3 of an open pre-adverse-action window

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed consent, background report, PDB regulatory-action capture, 1033 disposition memo and any commissioner written consent retained 7 years from termination in the compliance evidence repository, with restricted access

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any person engaged before a cleared screen, any 1033 prohibited person found active, and any undisclosed conviction discovered later is logged with the engagement dates and the removal or consent disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs every 1033 prohibited-person determination, every decision to seek commissioner written consent, and every removal from the business of insurance

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All employees hired and all producers or agencies contracted in the quarter, from HRIS new-hire records and the agency/producer management system contract log

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance - any person engaged in the business of insurance before a cleared screen, or any 1033 prohibited person active without commissioner written consent, is a fail and an immediate escalation to the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per hire and per contract; test runs quarterly over that quarter's hires and contracts, with 100% coverage of any candidate who had a criminal or regulatory hit

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have performed any sampled screen or 1033 determination and must have restricted-data access approved for the review

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly Fitness & Propriety test workpaper (hire/contract population, sample, re-performed PDB and 1033 analysis, exception schedule) in the compliance evidence repository under restricted access

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Screening register export with consent dates, clearance dates, 1033 dispositions and commissioner consent letters, producible for a DOI licensing or market conduct request within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Producer Compliance Manager answers DOI fitness inquiries; Regulatory Counsel clears any notification that a prohibited person was engaged and owns the 1033 written-consent correspondence

checklist.step: Capture written screening consent before any check is ordered
actions: At offer stage send the candidate the standalone FCRA disclosure and authorisation and the state-specific consent addenda through the recruiting system's e-signature step.
Send producers and agency principals the same package through the contracting pack in the agency/producer management system, alongside the licensing application.
Confirm the signed consent is dated before the screening order date - a check ordered before consent is void and must be re-run.
Attach the executed consent to the candidate or producer record and set the screening task to Ready to Order.
checklist.done: a dated, signed FCRA and state consent exists on the record before any check is ordered.

checklist.step: Order the background package scoped to the role and jurisdiction
actions: Order the standard package: county and federal criminal history for the last 7 years in every county of residence, national criminal database, sex-offender registry, OFAC/sanctions and adverse-media screen, employment and licence verification.
Add fingerprint-based criminal history through the state-designated vendor (IdentoGO or Fieldprint) for every state that requires it for licensure.
Add a credit report only where the role handles premium or claim funds and the state permits it, recording the permissible-purpose basis.
Record the vendor order reference and expected turnaround on the screening register row.
checklist.done: the ordered package matches the role and jurisdiction requirement, with fingerprints ordered wherever the state requires them.

checklist.step: Read the PDB regulatory-action and licence history for producers
actions: In NIPR Gateway open the PDB record for the NPN and read the Regulatory Actions section: action type, state, date, disposition and any licence revocation, suspension or surrender.
Read the licence history for lapses, non-renewals and terminations for cause reported by prior carriers.
Compare every action found to the candidate's own disclosure answers on the contracting questionnaire and list any omission.
Save the dated PDB capture into the screening file as the source for the fitness assessment.
checklist.done: the PDB regulatory-action and licence history is captured, compared to self-disclosure, and omissions are listed.

checklist.step: Assess every criminal record against the 1033 prohibition test
actions: For each conviction, record the offence, statute, jurisdiction, conviction date, felony/misdemeanour classification and disposition from the court record, not the vendor summary line.
Apply the 1033 test: is it a felony, and does it involve dishonesty or breach of trust (fraud, theft, embezzlement, forgery, false statements) or a felony under 18 U.S.C. 1033 itself.
Write a determination memo for each hit stating the test applied, the conclusion (prohibited / not prohibited) and the source document relied on.
Route every 'prohibited' conclusion and every borderline call to Regulatory Counsel before any decision reaches the candidate.
checklist.done: each criminal record has a written determination memo naming the offence, the 1033 test and the conclusion.

checklist.step: Confirm the 1033 determination with counsel and set the path forward
actions: Re-read the conviction record and the 1033 determination memo, and confirm or overturn the prohibited-person conclusion in writing.
Where the person is prohibited, decide whether the business will support a written-consent application to the commissioner of the person's resident state or decline engagement.
Where consent will be sought, name the sponsoring business owner and confirm the person may not engage in the business of insurance until consent is granted.
Stamp the memo with counsel name and date and attach it to the screening register row.
checklist.done: no prohibited-person conclusion stands without a dated counsel confirmation and a stated consent-or-decline path.

checklist.step: File the 1033 written-consent application where the path is consent
actions: Download the resident state's 1033 written-consent form and instructions from the DOI website and read the required exhibits.

Assemble the package: application form, certified court records including judgment and sentence, evidence of restitution and completion of sentence, letters of reference, the sponsoring carrier's supervision plan and the filing fee.
Submit to the DOI and record the submission date, method and any assigned reference number on the screening register.
Track the DOI response and file the granted consent letter, or the denial, in the screening file - engagement stays blocked until the letter is in hand.
checklist.done: a complete consent application is submitted with a tracked reference, and engagement remains blocked pending the DOI letter.

checklist.step: Run the FCRA adverse-action process before declining anyone on a report
actions: Send the pre-adverse-action notice with a copy of the consumer report and the CFPB Summary of Rights, and log the send date.
Hold the decision open for at least 5 business days so the candidate can dispute inaccuracies with the consumer reporting agency.
Where the candidate disputes, pause and re-read the corrected report before deciding; record the dispute outcome.
Issue the final adverse-action notice naming the agency and stating it did not make the decision, and file both notices on the candidate record.
checklist.done: every declined candidate has a pre-adverse notice, a documented dispute window of at least 5 business days, and a final notice on file.

checklist.step: Gate the start date and system access on a cleared screen
actions: Set the HRIS onboarding gate so the start date cannot be confirmed while the screening status is anything other than Cleared or Cleared with counsel memo.
Confirm identity, access and policy-system provisioning is triggered by the cleared status, never by the offer date.
For producers, confirm the agency/producer management system leaves the writing-eligibility flag off until both the licence and the screen are cleared.
Escalate any request to start ahead of clearance to the Head of Compliance in writing - verbal exceptions are not accepted.
checklist.done: no start date, system access or writing eligibility exists ahead of a recorded clearance.

checklist.step: Collect the annual attestation and re-screen on any reported event
actions: Issue the annual fitness attestation to all producers and licensed employees asking about new charges, convictions, regulatory actions and licence discipline since the last attestation.
Require reporting of any criminal charge or regulatory action within 30 days of occurrence, not at the next attestation.
On any positive answer, re-run the criminal and PDB checks and restart the 1033 determination.
Track non-responders weekly and suspend writing authority for any producer 30 days past the attestation due date.
checklist.done: every in-scope person has a current attestation on file and every positive answer has triggered a re-screen.

checklist.step: Monitor continuously for new regulatory actions and sanctions hits
actions: Subscribe the NPN list to PDB Alerts so a new regulatory action or licence status change generates a notification.
Re-run the sanctions and adverse-media screen for all producers and licensed staff monthly and clear hits within 5 business days.
Open a fitness review case for every new action, assess whether the underlying conduct triggers 1033, and record the outcome.
Feed confirmed actions to Distribution Operations so contract and appointment status follows the fitness decision.
checklist.done: PDB alerts and monthly sanctions rescreens are running with every hit dispositioned inside 5 business days.

checklist.step: Remove any prohibited person found already engaged
actions: On confirmation that an active person is 1033 prohibited without consent, suspend writing authority and system access the same day and record the timestamp.
Quantify the business written, claims handled or funds touched during the prohibited period and identify affected customers.
Terminate the contract or employment on counsel instruction and report the termination for cause to the states where the producer is appointed.
Open an exception record capturing dates, exposure, customer impact and the notification decision.
checklist.done: the prohibited person is suspended the same day, the exposure is quantified, and the termination and state notifications are recorded.

checklist.step: Handle screening data under privacy and access controls
actions: Store background reports and court records in the restricted screening library with access limited to named Compliance and HR roles.
Confirm the retention rule deletes reports 7 years after termination and that no copies persist in recruiting or email attachments.
Run a quarterly access recertification over the screening library and remove anyone without a current need.
Record the lawful basis and, for EU/UK candidates, the criminal-conviction data condition relied on.
checklist.done: screening data sits only in the restricted library with a recertified access list and a documented lawful basis.

checklist.step: Train recruiters and agency-relations staff on what stops a hire
actions: Deliver annual training covering the 1033 prohibition, the difference between a disqualifying felony and a spent misdemeanour, FCRA adverse-action steps and ban-the-box timing rules.
Include the escalation path and the rule that only Compliance and counsel make a prohibited-person call.
Assign the course in the LMS to all recruiters, HR Business Partners, Agency Relations Managers and Licensing Ops staff, with a 30-day completion window.
Report completion rates to the Head of Compliance and chase non-completers through their manager.
checklist.done: all recruiting, HR and agency-relations staff have current training with completion evidence in the LMS.

checklist.step: Report screening outcomes to the governance forum
actions: Report quarterly: screens ordered, cleared, hits assessed, prohibited-person determinations, consents sought and granted, and starts permitted ahead of clearance.
Trend turnaround time and highlight any business unit pressing for pre-clearance starts.
Present material fitness cases and their dispositions to the Compliance Committee.
File the pack and minutes as ICP 5 supervisory evidence in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a dated pack reports screen volumes, prohibited-person outcomes and any pre-clearance starts to the Compliance Committee.

checklist.step: Close the loop between screening, licensing and appointment records
actions: Reconcile the screening register to the contracted-producer list monthly and list any active producer with no cleared screen.
Confirm the producer master carries screening status, clearance date and attestation date as mandatory fields on every active record.
Block appointment submission in the licensing workflow where the screening status field is blank or expired.
Hand unreconciled records to the Producer Compliance Manager for same-month resolution.
checklist.done: every active producer record carries a cleared screening status and appointment submission is blocked without one.

testing.step: Build the population of people engaged in the quarter
actions: Extract from the HRIS every hire, rehire and internal transfer into an insurance-business role with a start date inside the quarter.
Extract from the agency/producer management system every producer and agency contracted or reactivated in the quarter.
Add contingent workers and temporary staff with access to policy, claims or premium systems so contractors cannot fall out of scope.
Reconcile the combined count to payroll starters and appointment submissions and resolve every difference before sampling.
testing.done: a combined hire, producer and contingent-worker population is extracted and reconciled to payroll and appointment records.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the screening register
actions: Match every population record to a screening register row on employee id or NPN.
List population records with no screening row - these are automatic exceptions with no judgement applied.
List screening rows with no population record and check whether a screen was run for someone never engaged, or a record was deleted.
Document both lists and their counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: every engaged person is matched to a screening record or listed as an unmatched exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample with mandatory strata
actions: Take 100% of records where the screen returned a criminal, sanctions or regulatory-action hit.
Take 100% of 1033 determinations and consent applications in the quarter.
Take 25 clean screens at random (seeded, reproducible) spread across employees, producers and agencies.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample covers all hits and 1033 cases plus 25 reproducible random clean screens.

testing.step: Re-perform the consent and package-scope check
actions: For each sampled record open the signed FCRA and state consent and compare its signature date to the vendor order date.
Confirm the package ordered matches the role and jurisdiction rule - fingerprints where the state requires them, credit only with a recorded permissible purpose.
Confirm criminal searches cover every county of residence in the look-back period, not just the current address.
Log as an exception any check ordered before consent, any missing fingerprint requirement, and any unsupported credit pull.
testing.done: consent timing and package scope are independently verified for every sampled record.

testing.step: Re-perform the PDB regulatory-action review for sampled producers
actions: Query the PDB for each sampled NPN and read the Regulatory Actions and licence history sections yourself before opening the screening file.
Compare what you find to the actions recorded in the screening file and to the producer's self-disclosure answers.
Treat any action visible in the PDB but absent from the screening assessment as an exception, including actions in non-appointed states.
Capture the PDB screen into the workpaper for each sampled producer.
testing.done: each sampled producer has an independent PDB reading compared to the screening file and the self-disclosure.

testing.step: Re-perform the 1033 prohibited-person analysis on every hit
actions: Read the underlying court record for each sampled conviction - charge, statute, felony/misdemeanour classification and disposition.
Reach your own conclusion on whether the offence is a felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust before reading the determination memo.
Compare to the recorded determination; a right answer supported by the wrong statute or by the vendor summary alone is still an exception.
Confirm every prohibited determination has a dated counsel sign-off that pre-dates any engagement decision.
testing.done: every sampled criminal hit has an independent 1033 conclusion compared to the recorded determination and its sign-off.

testing.step: Trace consent applications and clearance dates to primary evidence
actions: For each 1033 consent case, open the DOI submission, the exhibits list and the commissioner's response letter and confirm the granted scope covers the states where the person operates.
Compare the consent letter date to the person's first engagement date, first policy written or first claim handled.
Confirm any denial resulted in removal from the business of insurance, with a dated termination record.
Attach the consent or denial letter to the workpaper for each case.
testing.done: each consent case traces to a commissioner letter whose date and scope are compared to actual engagement.

testing.step: Recompute the adverse-action and start-date gates
actions: For each declined candidate, recompute the interval between the pre-adverse-action notice and the final notice and confirm at least 5 business days elapsed.
For each hire, compare the screening clearance date to the HRIS start date and to the first system-access provisioning timestamp.
For each producer, compare clearance date to the first application written with that producer as writing agent.
Log every start, access grant or sale that pre-dates clearance, with the number of days of exposure.
testing.done: adverse-action intervals and clearance-versus-engagement dates are recomputed with all exposure days quantified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception recording the person, role, what failed and whether any customer-facing activity occurred before clearance.
Assign a root cause (consent captured late, package mis-scoped, PDB not read, business pressure on start date, no re-screen after attestation hit) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any prohibited person found engaged, open a counsel-led notification assessment.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue reference, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the pre-clearance engagement count, the hit-assessment completion rate and the 1033 determination accuracy rate from the re-performance results.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references behind each figure.
Have an Internal Auditor who performed none of the sampled screens sign the workpaper under restricted access.
Report the result and any prohibited-person engagement to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the pre-clearance engagement count, determination accuracy, conclusion and committee reporting date.

In-scope systems.value: NIPR PDB appointment and licence data reconciled against the agency/producer management system roster and the commission payee file

Compliance procedure documented.value: Producer Roster Reconciliation Procedure - quarterly PDB bulk extract, three-way match to contracts and commission payees, break classification, correction transactions and sign-off

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs the quarterly reconciliation as complete and approves the disposition of every aged break carried forward

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The full appointment universe for the quarter - every active PDB appointment for each writing company plus every active producer contract and every commission payee paid in the quarter

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero unexplained breaks at sign-off; any business written before an appointment was effective, or any commission paid to an unappointed producer, is a fail regardless of later correction

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly Producer Roster Reconciliation test workpaper (independent PDB extract, three-way match, break re-performance, NIPR trace) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Reconciliation report with break schedule, NIPR transaction IDs and appointment effective dates, producible for a market conduct exam producer-licensing standard within 10 business days

checklist.step: Pull the regulator-side appointment universe
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Reports > Producer Database (PDB) and run the appointment report for every writing company FEIN and NAIC company code in the group.
Export appointments with NPN, producer name, state, company code, appointment effective date, appointment status and lines of authority as of quarter end.
Run the companion licence report so each appointment can later be tested against a live licence in the same state and line.
Save both extracts dated as of quarter end - the reconciliation must use a fixed as-of date, not a rolling query.
checklist.done: dated PDB appointment and licence extracts exist for every writing company as of the quarter-end date.

checklist.step: Pull the internal roster of who is contracted to sell
actions: Extract every producer and agency with an active or pending-termination contract as at quarter end, with NPN, contract status, contract effective and termination dates, writing companies and states authorised.
Include downline producers under agency contracts so agency-hierarchy sellers are not missed.
Flag records with a missing or malformed NPN and fix them before the match - an unmatched key manufactures false breaks.
Hand the extract and its record count to Licensing Ops with a signed completeness statement.
checklist.done: a dated, NPN-keyed contract roster with a signed record count is delivered to Licensing Ops.

checklist.step: Pull the commission payee file as the third leg of the match
actions: Extract every payee paid commission in the quarter with NPN or agency tax id, state of the underlying policy, writing company and amount paid.
Split first-year, renewal and override commissions so an override to an unappointed upline is visible.
Reconcile the extract total to the general-ledger commission expense for the quarter and note any difference.
Deliver the file to Licensing Ops with the reconciliation note attached.
checklist.done: a commission payee file tied to the GL commission expense is delivered with first-year, renewal and override splits.

checklist.step: Run the three-way match and classify every break
actions: Match PDB appointments, contract roster and commission payees on NPN plus writing company plus state.

Classify each break: appointed-not-contracted, contracted-not-appointed, paid-not-appointed, appointment line of authority narrower than the business written, or licence expired with appointment still active.
Age each break from the earliest evidence date (first application, first commission payment or appointment effective date).
Produce the break schedule with owner and target correction date per row and circulate it to Distribution Operations and Commission Operations.
checklist.done: a classified, aged break schedule exists with an owner and target date on every row.

checklist.step: Test each contracted-not-appointed break for business already written
actions: For every contracted-not-appointed producer, query new business by writing-agent NPN, state and application date since the contract effective date.

Where an application exists, read the state's appointment rule - most appointment-required states demand the appointment within 15 days of the first application, some allow appointment at the time of the first submission.
Compute whether the appointment window has already been breached and record the number of days past due.
Flag breached rows for immediate appointment filing and for counsel review of any premium written outside the window.
checklist.done: every contracted-not-appointed producer is tested for written business and any breached appointment window is quantified in days.

checklist.step: File the corrective appointment transactions
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Appointments > Appointment Submission, select the writing company and state, and submit the NPN batch with the correct lines of authority.
Pay the state appointment fee and record the transaction ID, submission date and requested effective date on the break row.
Re-query the PDB after five business days and confirm the appointment shows Active with the expected effective date.
Close the break row only once the PDB confirms the appointment, not at submission.
checklist.done: each missing appointment is filed with a NIPR transaction ID and confirmed Active in the PDB before the break is closed.

checklist.step: Terminate appointments for producers no longer contracted
actions: For every appointed-not-contracted break, confirm with Distribution Operations the contract termination date and whether the termination was for cause.

In NIPR Gateway open Appointments > Termination and submit the termination with the correct reason code and effective date within the state's notice window, commonly 30 days from the termination decision.
Where the termination was for cause, prepare the state-required written statement of the reason and any supporting documentation, and route it through Regulatory Counsel before sending.
Record the transaction ID and confirm the PDB appointment status flips to Terminated.
checklist.done: every appointed-not-contracted producer is terminated in NIPR within the state notice window with the reason code recorded.

checklist.step: Stop and recover commissions paid to unappointed payees
actions: Place a payment hold on every paid-not-appointed payee and quantify amounts already paid by policy and state.
Confirm with Regulatory Counsel whether the state permits payment of renewal commissions to a terminated producer and, if not, redirect to the licensed agent of record.
Raise the recovery or reallocation entries and confirm the general-ledger posting.
Release the hold only when the appointment is confirmed Active in the PDB or the payee is corrected.
checklist.done: unappointed payees are on hold, amounts are quantified, and each is either corrected or recovered with a GL entry.

checklist.step: Fix the line-of-authority and licence mismatches
actions: Compare each appointment's lines of authority to the products the producer actually sold in that state during the quarter.
Where the producer sold outside the appointed lines, add the missing line to the appointment and check the underlying licence carries that line first.
Where the licence is expired but the appointment is still active, suspend writing authority and route the producer into the renewal process.
Record each mismatch, its cause and the fix on the break schedule.
checklist.done: no active appointment carries lines narrower than the business sold, and no appointment sits on an expired licence.

checklist.step: Correct the root data so the same break does not recur
actions: Trace recurring breaks to their source - duplicate producer records, NPN typed rather than validated, contracts loaded without a writing-company scope, terminations recorded in HR but not in the producer master.
Add or tighten the validation rule (NPN format and PDB existence check at contract creation, mandatory writing-company scope, termination workflow that pushes to Licensing Ops automatically).
Merge duplicate producer records and repoint policies and commissions to the surviving record.
Record the data fix and the control change against the break so the next reconciliation can prove it worked.
checklist.done: each recurring break class has a named root cause, a system validation or workflow change, and merged duplicate records.

checklist.step: Reconcile the non-US intermediary registers as well
actions: For UK business, reconcile the appointed-representative and broker list to the FCA Financial Services Register, checking permissions cover the classes placed.
For Canadian business, reconcile agent records to the provincial regulator licence registers (for example FSRA Ontario, AMF Quebec) and confirm errors-and-omissions cover is current.
Record any intermediary acting without a current registration or permission as a break with the same classification scheme.
Report cross-border breaks separately so the group supervisor view under ICP 18 is complete.
checklist.done: non-US intermediary registers are reconciled and any unregistered intermediary is logged in the same break schedule.

checklist.step: Produce and sign the quarterly reconciliation report
actions: Assemble the report: as-of date, record counts from all three sources, match rate, break counts by class, corrections filed, aged breaks carried forward with reasons.
State explicitly whether any business was written or commission paid outside a valid appointment during the quarter.
Sign the report and route it to the Head of Compliance within 20 business days of quarter end.
File the report with the underlying extracts and NIPR confirmations under the quarter's evidence folder.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation report with counts, match rate, break classes and carried-forward reasons is filed within 20 business days.

checklist.step: Escalate aged and repeat breaks
actions: Review any break older than one quarter and any break class that recurs across two consecutive quarters.
Require a written remediation plan from the owning function with a completion date, not a rolling explanation.
Escalate to the Compliance Committee where unappointed business or unrecovered commissions exceed the agreed materiality.
Track the plan to completion in the GRC issue record and re-test at the next reconciliation.
checklist.done: every aged or repeat break has a written, dated remediation plan tracked as a GRC issue.

checklist.step: Report reconciliation results into distribution governance
actions: Publish the quarterly dashboard: match rate by state and writing company, break counts by class, days-to-correct and unappointed premium.
Highlight the three states and three agencies driving most breaks and name their owners.
Present at the Distribution Compliance forum alongside the licence renewal pack so licensing and appointment risk are read together.
File the pack and minutes as ICP 18 evidence.
checklist.done: a dated dashboard and minutes show match rate, break classes, days-to-correct and named owners.

checklist.step: Retain the reconciliation evidence set
actions: File the PDB extracts, roster and commission files, break schedule, NIPR confirmations and signed report under the quarter.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the reconciliation date.
Confirm the index supports retrieval by NPN, state, writing company and quarter for exam response.
Verify every break row on the schedule links to its correction evidence before the folder is locked.
checklist.done: the quarter's reconciliation evidence is filed, retention-labelled, indexed by NPN and state, with every break linked to its correction.

testing.step: Rebuild the appointment population independently
actions: Run your own PDB appointment extract for every writing company as of the same quarter-end date used by Licensing Ops.
Compare your record count and company-code coverage to the extract used in the reconciliation and investigate any difference.
Confirm no writing company was omitted by checking the group's licensed-entity list from Statutory Reporting.
Sign the population as complete with the extract timestamp.
testing.done: an independent PDB extract covering every writing company reconciles to the population used in the reconciliation.

testing.step: Re-run the three-way match on the source files
actions: Take the raw contract roster and commission payee files and re-run the match on NPN plus writing company plus state yourself.
Compare your break count by class to the reconciliation's break schedule and list any break the reconciliation missed or suppressed.
Check the match keys for silent losses - trimmed leading zeros on NPN, state code case differences, agency tax id used where NPN was required.
Document the re-run counts alongside the reported counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independently re-run match reproduces or contradicts the reported break counts, with key-handling defects listed.

testing.step: Draw the break and clean-match sample
actions: Take 100% of breaks classed as paid-not-appointed and 100% of breaks aged over one quarter.
Take 25 breaks at random across the remaining classes and 15 clean matches to test for false clears.
Record the seed, population sizes by class and selection date for reproducibility.
Confirm the sample spans at least six states and both retail and agency-hierarchy channels.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all high-risk breaks, 25 random breaks and 15 clean matches is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the appointment status check in the PDB
actions: For each sampled row query the PDB directly and read appointment status, effective date, termination date and lines of authority before opening the break schedule.
Compare to the recorded classification; any status or date difference is an exception including a correct classification supported by a stale extract.
For clean-match rows confirm the appointment genuinely exists and is Active - a false clear is more serious than a logged break.
Capture the PDB screen into the workpaper for every sampled row.
testing.done: each sampled row has an independent PDB reading captured and compared to its recorded classification.

testing.step: Trace corrections to real NIPR transactions
actions: Search each recorded NIPR transaction ID and confirm it matches the sampled NPN, writing company, state and transaction type.
Confirm appointment effective dates and termination effective dates on the confirmation agree with the break schedule.
Confirm the fee paid agrees to the state's published appointment or termination fee.
Flag any break closed without a traceable transaction as an exception.
testing.done: every closed break traces to a genuine NIPR transaction with agreed dates, type and fee.

testing.step: Test business written against appointment effective dates
actions: Extract all new business in the quarter with application date, state, writing company and writing-agent NPN.
Join to the PDB appointment history and flag every application whose date falls before the appointment effective date in an appointment-required state.
Quantify premium and commission on each flagged application and check it appears on the break schedule.
Escalate flagged business not already identified by the reconciliation as a control failure, not a data difference.
testing.done: business written outside a valid appointment is identified by system join, quantified and matched to logged breaks.

testing.step: Recompute the statutory appointment and termination clocks
actions: For each sampled appointment, recompute the days between the first application date and the appointment effective date and compare to the state's window (commonly 15 days).

For each sampled termination, recompute the days between the termination decision date recorded in the producer master and the NIPR termination submission date and compare to the state's notice window (commonly 30 days).
For terminations for cause, confirm the state-required written reason statement was sent within the state's deadline.
Log every clock breach with the number of days late and the state cite relied on.
testing.done: appointment and termination clocks are recomputed per sampled row with every breach quantified in days against a cited rule.

testing.step: Test commission payments against appointment status
actions: Take the quarter's commission payments and join each payee to their appointment status at the payment date.
List payments made while the payee had no active appointment in the policy's state, split by first-year, renewal and override.
Confirm each listed payment is on hold, recovered or supported by a counsel opinion that the state permits renewal payment post-termination.
Agree the total of unsupported payments to the recovery entries posted in the general ledger.
testing.done: commission payments to unappointed payees are quantified and reconciled to holds, recoveries or a cited counsel opinion.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception recording NPN, state, writing company, break class, days late and financial exposure.
Assign a root cause (contract loaded without appointment trigger, termination not pushed from HR, duplicate producer record, NPN key defect, extract taken on the wrong as-of date) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and open a counsel-led self-report assessment for any unappointed premium above the agreed threshold.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's reconciliation test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue reference, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the independently verified match rate, the count of breaks missed by the reconciliation, and unappointed premium and commission totals.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references for every figure.
Have an Internal Auditor who neither performed the reconciliation nor filed the corrections sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any unappointed-business breach to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the verified match rate, missed-break count, unappointed exposure, conclusion and committee reporting date.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - IAIS ICP 19 (Conduct of Business), Standard 19.11 on documented policies and procedures, read with ICP 21 (Countering Fraud), Standards 21.1-21.2 and ICP 22 (AML/CFT) on written AML/CFT policies consistent with the FATF Recommendations; each mapped to the corresponding local rule in the jurisdictions the group writes in

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with Regulatory Counsel concurrence; each individual conduct procedure approved by its named business owner and re-approved annually

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Every procedure reviewed and re-approved within 12 months of its last approval date; out-of-cycle updates completed within 60 days of a regulatory change taking effect, and within 30 days where the change carries an immediate compliance date

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC workflow notifies the procedure owner at 90, 60 and 30 days before the review-due date and escalates to the Head of Compliance at 15 days overdue
