Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Overdue reviews, procedures with no named owner, ICP standards with no mapped procedure and procedures contradicted by observed practice are each logged with an owner and a correction date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every overdue-review exception and every mapping gap where an ICP standard had no procedure covering it

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The full conduct procedure inventory in the GRC platform plus the ICP 19/21/22 standard list, so both directions are tested - procedures without a mapping and standards without a procedure

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of conduct procedures within their 12-month review window and 100% of mapped ICP standards covered by a live procedure; any procedure whose stated process contradicts observed practice is a fail regardless of approval status

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is an annual review cycle; test runs annually across the whole inventory with a semi-annual interim check on overdue reviews and on procedures touched by a regulatory change

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not own or have authored any sampled procedure and reports through Internal Audit, not through Compliance

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual Conduct Procedure Review test workpaper (inventory extract, ICP mapping matrix, sample, walkthrough notes, exception schedule) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Procedure inventory export with owners, approval dates, version history and the ICP-to-procedure mapping matrix, producible for a supervisory review or market conduct exam within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager supplies procedures to examiners; Regulatory Counsel reviews any procedure released outside the group and any statement about a procedure that was not in force at the examined period

checklist.step: Build the ICP-to-procedure mapping matrix
actions: List every ICP standard the group treats as conduct-relevant - ICP 19 Standards 19.1 to 19.13, ICP 21 Standards 21.1 to 21.6, ICP 22 Standards 22.1 to 22.7 - as rows in the GRC obligation register.
Map each standard to the local rule that implements it in each writing jurisdiction, so the procedure has a concrete compliance date and not just a principle.
Attach the procedure or procedures that satisfy each standard, recording document id, version and owner.
List every standard with no attached procedure as a mapping gap and assign an owner and a drafting date.
checklist.done: every conduct ICP standard has either a mapped, versioned procedure or a logged gap with an owner and drafting date.

checklist.step: Name an accountable owner for every procedure
actions: Set the owner field on each procedure record to a named individual in the business function that performs the process, not to Compliance by default.
Set a second-line reviewer for each procedure and record the approval body (Compliance Committee, Product Governance Forum, Claims Leadership).
Confirm with each named owner in writing that they accept the review, accuracy and training obligations for their procedure.
Reassign any procedure whose owner has left or moved before the review cycle opens.
checklist.done: every procedure record carries a live named business owner, a second-line reviewer and a recorded acceptance.

checklist.step: Open the annual review cycle and issue the review packs
actions: Run the GRC report of procedures whose last approval date is more than nine months old and schedule each into the cycle.

Issue each owner a review pack containing the current version, the mapped ICP standards and local rules, regulatory changes logged since last approval, and the complaints, exam findings and QA results touching that process.
Set the review due date and confirm the 90/60/30-day reminders are armed in the workflow.
Publish the cycle plan to the Compliance Committee so slippage is visible from the start.
checklist.done: every procedure due within the year is scheduled with an issued review pack, a due date and armed reminders.

checklist.step: Review the sales suitability and disclosure procedures against ICP 19
actions: Re-read the procedure against ICP 19 Standards 19.5 to 19.8 on information to customers, advice and suitability, plus the local best-interest rule for annuity and investment products.

Confirm the procedure states the suitability information collected, the documented basis for a recommendation, who may override a declination, and the record kept of the customer's own decision to proceed against advice.
Confirm the disclosure timing is specific - point-of-sale illustration, free-look period length and replacement notice deadlines - rather than 'as required'.
Redline the gaps and route to the Head of Distribution and Regulatory Counsel for comment.
checklist.done: the suitability and disclosure procedures state the information collected, the recommendation basis, override authority and each disclosure deadline.

checklist.step: Review the complaints-handling procedure against ICP 19 and local rules
actions: Re-read the procedure against ICP 19 Standard 19.13 on complaints handling and each jurisdiction's acknowledgement and response deadlines (for example 15 days to acknowledge a DOI complaint in most US states, 8 weeks to final response under UK DISP).
Confirm it defines what counts as a complaint, how DOI-forwarded complaints are separated from direct ones, the root-cause coding scheme, and the escalation of trends to Product and Claims.
Confirm it names who signs a final response and the ombudsman or DOI referral wording required.
Update the deadline table with the current jurisdiction values and cite each source.
checklist.done: the complaints procedure defines complaint scope, per-jurisdiction deadlines with citations, root-cause coding and escalation.

checklist.step: Review the fraud procedure against ICP 21
actions: Re-read the anti-fraud procedure against ICP 21 Standards 21.1 to 21.2 requiring policies, procedures and controls proportionate to assessed fraud risk across products, channels and processes.
Confirm it lists the current fraud typologies with their detection indicators, the referral thresholds to SIU, and the state fraud-bureau reporting deadlines and forms.
Confirm the procedure requires the fraud risk assessment to be refreshed at least annually and after any new product or channel launch.
Add any typology emerging from the year's SIU casework - synthetic identity, agent-assisted application fraud, organised claim rings - with its indicator set.
checklist.done: the fraud procedure carries a current typology list with indicators, SIU referral thresholds and fraud-bureau reporting deadlines.

checklist.step: Review the AML/CFT procedure against ICP 22 and the FATF Recommendations
actions: Re-read the AML/CFT procedure against ICP 22 Standards 22.1 to 22.7 and confirm it applies a risk-based approach across customers, products, channels and geographies as required by Standard 22.3.

Confirm the procedure sets the customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence and simplified due diligence triggers, the PEP and sanctions screening cadence, and the SAR decision and filing route with its deadline.
Confirm coverage of the life and investment product lines specifically, including beneficiary due diligence at payout, and the treatment of third-party premium payers.
Route the redline to the MLRO equivalent in each regulated entity so local additions are captured in one version.
checklist.done: the AML/CFT procedure documents the risk-based CDD/EDD triggers, screening cadence, beneficiary due diligence and SAR route with deadlines.

checklist.step: Walk the procedure against how the work is actually done
actions: Sit with two practitioners per procedure and walk a live case end to end, noting each system screen and decision point they use.
Mark every step in the written procedure that no longer matches the system, the approval limit or the hand-off.
Note steps performed in practice that appear nowhere in the procedure, especially manual workarounds.
Give the owner a written walkthrough note listing each divergence and whether the procedure or the practice must change.
checklist.done: each reviewed procedure has a walkthrough note listing every divergence between written steps and observed practice.

checklist.step: Redline, version and route the procedure for approval
actions: Apply the redline in the controlled template, incrementing the version and completing the change-summary table with what changed, why and the driving citation.
Route to the named business owner and second-line reviewer for electronic approval, with Regulatory Counsel added where the change interprets a rule.
Confirm the approval record captures approver name, role, date and version - an email 'looks fine' is not an approval record.
Publish the approved version and retire the previous one so only one version is live.
checklist.done: each updated procedure has an incremented version, a completed change summary, recorded approvals and a single live published copy.

checklist.step: Push procedure changes into training and job aids
actions: For every material change, update the affected course, job aid and quick-reference card before the effective date.
Assign a read-and-acknowledge or short assessment to the population that performs the process, with a 30-day completion window.
Update the new-joiner onboarding curriculum so new staff learn the current version, not the superseded one.
Report completion by team to the procedure owner and chase non-completers through their manager.
checklist.done: every material change has updated training assigned to the performing population with tracked completion.

checklist.step: Trigger out-of-cycle updates on regulatory change
actions: Screen incoming bulletins, model-law adoptions, IAIS application-paper updates and supervisory statements weekly and tag each to the affected ICP standards.
Where a change bites, open an out-of-cycle procedure change with a 60-day completion date, or 30 days where the rule has an immediate compliance date.
Notify the procedure owner and Learning & Development the same week so the training change starts in parallel.
Record the change, effective date, citation and the resulting procedure version in the regulatory change log.
checklist.done: every applicable regulatory change has a tagged, dated out-of-cycle procedure update with a citation in the change log.

checklist.step: Close the mapping gaps by drafting the missing procedures
actions: Take each ICP standard flagged as unmapped and decide whether it needs its own procedure or a named section inside an existing one.
Draft to the controlled template with the standard, the local rule, the process steps, the control points and the evidence produced.
Have the performing function confirm the drafted steps are what they will actually do before approval, not after.
Close the gap record only when the approved procedure is published and mapped in the GRC register.
checklist.done: every mapping gap is closed by a published, mapped procedure confirmed by the performing function.

checklist.step: Collect the annual owner attestation
actions: Issue each procedure owner an attestation that their procedure is accurate, in use, mapped to current rules, and supported by trained staff.
Require any negative answer to name the divergence and a correction date rather than a free-text caveat.
Escalate non-responders to their function head at 15 days overdue and to the Head of Compliance at 30 days.
Store the completed attestations against the procedure record as review evidence.
checklist.done: every procedure carries a completed owner attestation, with negative answers converted into dated corrections.

checklist.step: Report inventory health to the Compliance Committee
actions: Report procedures in force, reviewed on time, overdue, unmapped standards, out-of-cycle changes and training completion.
Show the ICP coverage heat map so a standard with no procedure is visible to the committee, not buried in an appendix.
Take committee decisions on any procedure the business proposes not to maintain, and minute the rationale.
File the pack and minutes as ICP 19 governance evidence.
checklist.done: a dated committee pack shows on-time review rate, coverage heat map, overdue items and minuted decisions.

checklist.step: Retain every version so a past state can be reproduced
actions: Archive each superseded version with its approval record, redline and effective-from and effective-to dates.
Apply the 7-years-from-supersession retention label.
Test retrieval by asking the repository for the version of the complaints procedure in force on a stated past date and confirm exactly one version returns.
Confirm the archive is indexed by procedure id, ICP standard and effective period for exam response.
checklist.done: any procedure version in force on a given past date can be retrieved uniquely, with its approval record and retention label.

testing.step: Extract the procedure inventory and the standard list as the population
actions: Export every conduct procedure record with id, title, owner, last approval date, next review date, version and mapped ICP standards.
Export the ICP 19/21/22 standard list from the obligation register as the second population so coverage can be tested in both directions.
Reconcile the procedure count to the published document set in the document management repository and investigate documents live in the repository but absent from the register.
Sign both populations as complete with the extract date and counts.
testing.done: procedure and standard populations are extracted, reconciled to the published document set, and signed as complete.

testing.step: Test coverage in both directions
actions: List every ICP standard with no mapped live procedure and confirm each appears as a logged gap with an owner and date.
List every live procedure with no mapped standard and determine whether it is genuinely out of scope or a mapping omission.
Check that a standard mapped to a procedure is actually addressed in that procedure's text, not merely referenced in a header.
Record unmapped standards, unmapped procedures and hollow mappings separately in the workpaper.
testing.done: coverage is tested in both directions with unmapped standards, unmapped procedures and hollow mappings listed separately.

testing.step: Draw the sample across risk areas
actions: Take 100% of procedures covering AML/CFT, suitability, complaints and claims handling given their exam exposure.
Take 12 further procedures at random (seeded, reproducible) from the remaining inventory.
Include every procedure that had an out-of-cycle change in the year and every procedure with an overdue review.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers the four high-risk areas, 12 random procedures and all out-of-cycle and overdue items.

testing.step: Recompute the review-window arithmetic
actions: For each sampled procedure recompute months elapsed between the last approval date and today and compare to the 12-month window.
For out-of-cycle changes recompute days between the regulatory effective date and the approved version date and compare to the 60-day, or 30-day immediate-compliance, requirement.
Confirm the GRC next-review-date field was actually recalculated on approval rather than carried forward.
Log every window breach with the number of days late.
testing.done: review windows and out-of-cycle change clocks are recomputed with every breach quantified in days.

testing.step: Re-read sampled procedures against the current regulatory text
actions: Open the current ICP text and the mapped local rule and read the sampled procedure against both.
Check specifics rather than tone - stated deadlines, thresholds, record-retention periods, who may approve exceptions.
Flag any procedure citing a superseded bulletin, a repealed rule or a deadline that has since changed.
Record each finding with the correct current requirement so the owner has an actionable correction.
testing.done: each sampled procedure is read against current ICP and local text with every stale deadline, threshold or citation identified.

testing.step: Walk sampled procedures against live cases
actions: For each sampled procedure select three completed cases from the period - a complaint, a suitability review, a claim, an SAR decision as applicable.
Trace each case through the procedure's stated steps and confirm the evidence the procedure promises actually exists on the file.
Interview one practitioner without the procedure in front of them and compare their described process to the written one.
Log any step performed differently, skipped, or performed in a system the procedure does not name.
testing.done: each sampled procedure is walked against three live cases and one practitioner interview, with divergences logged.

testing.step: Test approval and version control
actions: For each sampled procedure open the approval record and confirm approver name, role, date and version are captured and that the approver held the authority in the approval matrix.
Confirm exactly one live version is published and that superseded versions are retired, not merely renamed.
Request the version in force on a stated past date and confirm the repository returns one unambiguous document.
Flag any procedure published without a recorded approval or with two live versions.
testing.done: approval records, single-live-version control and point-in-time retrieval are verified for every sampled procedure.

testing.step: Test that training followed the procedure change
actions: For each materially changed procedure, pull the assigned course or acknowledgement and its completion report.
Compare the assigned population to the actual list of staff performing the process from the HRIS role data.
Recompute completion rate and confirm assignment happened on or before the procedure's effective date.
Flag changes with no training, incomplete population coverage or completion after the effective date.
testing.done: training assignment, population coverage and completion timing are verified against each material procedure change.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception recording the procedure id, ICP standard, the defect and the conduct risk it creates.
Assign a root cause (owner vacancy, review skipped, regulatory change not screened, mapping never built, training not triggered) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and require a re-approved version, not just an acknowledgement, where the text is wrong.
Carry every open issue into the next annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue reference, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-time review rate, ICP coverage percentage and the count of procedures contradicted by observed practice.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references behind each figure.
Have an Internal Auditor who owns and authored none of the sampled procedures sign the workpaper.
Report the result and the coverage heat map to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the on-time review rate, ICP coverage, practice divergences, conclusion and committee reporting date.

checklist.step: Read the data year's Data Call and Definitions before touching any data
actions: Download the current MCAS Data Call and Definitions and the participating-states list for each reportable line from the NAIC MCAS page on iSite+.
Diff this year's definitions against last year's element by element and list every new, deleted or re-worded element with its interrogatory number.
Read the line-specific instructions for the lines the company writes and note any changed inclusion rule such as a new treatment of partial-year policies or reopened claims.
Circulate the change list to the Claims, Policy Administration and Complaints data owners and file the dated definitions PDF as the year's baseline.
checklist.done: the data year's definitions are filed with a documented element-by-element change list circulated to every data owner.

checklist.step: Determine participation state by state and line
actions: Extract direct written premium by state, line and writing company for the data year from the statutory reporting system and agree it to the Annual Statement state pages.

Apply the MCAS participation threshold for each line (direct written premium of 50,000 US dollars or more in the state, or the state's own stated threshold) and mark each state-and-line as reportable or not.
Check the participating-states list, since a state must itself participate in that line's data call before a filing is due.
Produce the scoping matrix showing state, line, writing company, premium, threshold and the reportable decision, and have the Statutory Reporting Manager confirm the premium figures.
checklist.done: a signed scoping matrix shows premium, threshold and a reportable/not-reportable decision for every state and line.

checklist.step: Map every MCAS element to a source field and owner
actions: Build the element mapping: for each interrogatory, name the source system, table and field, the inclusion filter, the date basis and the data owner.

Resolve definition-to-system mismatches explicitly - for example whether a claim closed without payment includes a claim closed as a duplicate, or whether policies in force are counted at 31 December or as an average.
Record any element that cannot be produced from a system and must be assembled manually, with the manual procedure and its reviewer.
Have each data owner sign their section of the mapping before extraction begins.
checklist.done: every MCAS element has a named source field, inclusion filter, date basis and an owner signature on the mapping.

checklist.step: Freeze the source data and run the extract
actions: Take the 31 January snapshot of policy administration, claims, complaints and lawsuit data for the data year and lock it as the MCAS reporting layer.
Run the extraction jobs per element and write results into the MCAS staging tables with a run id, row counts and the query text stored alongside.
Confirm re-running the extract on the frozen snapshot reproduces identical figures before any review begins.
Publish the run id and row counts to Regulatory Reporting as the basis for every downstream number.
checklist.done: a locked snapshot and a reproducible extract run exist, with row counts and stored query text per element.

checklist.step: Tie the extract back to the systems of record
actions: Reconcile policies in force and new business counts to the policy administration production reports for the same state, line and date basis.
Reconcile claim counts and paid amounts to the claims platform reporting and to the statutory Schedule P or the equivalent paid-loss data.
Reconcile complaint counts to the complaints register and separately to the NAIC Complaints Database Search figures for the company.
Document each tie-out with the compared figures, the difference and the explanation; anything over 0.5% goes back to the data owner before proceeding.
checklist.done: policy, claim and complaint elements are tied to their systems of record with every difference over 0.5% explained or fixed.

checklist.step: Run the definitional validations the NAIC blank will apply
actions: Apply the internal validation set that mirrors the MCAS edit checks - claims closed with payment plus closed without payment plus open must reconcile to claims received plus open at start, and lawsuit counts must not exceed claims closed.
Check every ratio-driving pair for impossible combinations such as claims paid with zero claims received, or median days to settle populated where no claims closed.
Confirm date-basis consistency across elements so that a policy counted in force is on the same 31 December basis everywhere it appears.
Return a validation report per state and line with pass/fail per rule and hand failures to the data owner with a fix date.
checklist.done: every state-and-line extract passes the internal edit set, or each failure has a dated owner and fix.

checklist.step: Review year-over-year and peer variances before filing
actions: Compare each element and each derived ratio to the prior data year by state and line and list every movement over 20% or over the agreed absolute threshold.
Obtain a business explanation for each movement from Claims, Underwriting or Complaints - a rate change, a book transfer, a system migration, a change in claim closing practice.
Compare key ratios to the prior year's published MCAS ratio benchmarks so an outlier is understood before a regulator asks.
Record each explanation, its source and its owner in the variance log attached to the filing package.
checklist.done: every material year-over-year movement has a named business explanation, source and owner in the variance log.

checklist.step: Have the business owners review their own numbers
actions: Send the claims elements to the Claims Director, the complaints elements to the Complaints Manager and the policy elements to the Policy Admin Ops Lead for review against what they know of the year.
Ask each reviewer to confirm in writing that the figures are consistent with their own management reporting, or to state the difference.
Resolve every stated difference before the attestation package is built rather than footnoting it.
File the reviewer confirmations in the filing package.
checklist.done: each business owner has confirmed their elements in writing, with all stated differences resolved before attestation.

checklist.step: Build the submission files in the NAIC required format
actions: Generate the MCAS submission file per line in the NAIC-specified layout, keyed by NAIC company code, state and data year.
Load the file into the MCAS application on iSite+ and run the built-in validation, resolving every error and reading every warning rather than dismissing it.
Complete the interrogatories and any required narrative or comment fields, keeping the wording consistent across states.
Save the validated draft and export the draft blank for the attestation package.
checklist.done: a validated MCAS draft exists in the NAIC application for every reportable state and line with no unresolved errors.

checklist.step: Assemble and sign the attestation package
actions: Assemble the package: scoping matrix, element mapping, extract run ids, tie-out schedules, validation report, variance log, business-owner confirmations and the draft blanks.
Review the package against the attestation wording, which asserts the data is complete and accurate to the best of the signer's knowledge and prepared per the Data Call and Definitions.
Obtain the officer signature required by the data call and record signer name, title and date.
File the signed package by 15 April so the submission is not the first time anyone senior sees the numbers.
checklist.done: a signed attestation package with scoping, mapping, tie-outs, validations and variance explanations is filed by 15 April.

checklist.step: Submit each state filing and capture the confirmation
actions: Submit each state-and-line filing in the MCAS application no later than 25 April, keeping five business days of buffer before the 30 April deadline.
Download the submission confirmation for each filing and record the confirmation number, submission timestamp, state, line and company code in the filing log.
Re-open the MCAS application after submission and confirm each filing shows status Submitted for every state on the scoping matrix.
Report any state on the scoping matrix without a submitted filing to the Regulatory Reporting Manager the same day.
checklist.done: every reportable state-and-line shows a Submitted status with a captured confirmation number before 30 April.

checklist.step: Handle state follow-ups and any required refiling
actions: Log every state query, NAIC help-desk message or data-quality challenge with the state, element and the response deadline stated in the query.
Investigate to the element mapping and the frozen snapshot, and answer with the tie-out evidence rather than a re-derived figure.
Where a restatement is required, refile through the MCAS application, record the reason and the changed elements, and note the refiling on the original filing log row.
Have the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager sign off every restatement before it is refiled.
checklist.done: every state query is logged, answered from the frozen evidence within its deadline, and any refiling carries a signed reason.

checklist.step: Feed the reported ratios back into conduct monitoring
actions: Compute the ratios examiners read from MCAS - claim denial rate, percentage of claims closed without payment, median days to settle, complaint ratio, lawsuit rate, replacement and free-look rates.
Compare each ratio to the industry distribution published for the line and flag any state where the company sits in the outlier tail.
Open a conduct review for each outlier state and line, with an owner and a completion date, before an examiner selects it.
Report the outlier list to the Compliance Committee alongside the filing confirmation.
checklist.done: MCAS ratios are computed, benchmarked, and every outlier state-and-line has an owned conduct review.

checklist.step: Run the post-filing lessons-learned and fix the pipeline
actions: Hold a post-filing review within four weeks of submission covering late milestones, manual elements, tie-out failures and validation errors.
Convert each recurring manual element into a system-sourced element with a named delivery date, so next year's package needs fewer manual assemblies.
Update the element mapping and procedure with the definitional decisions made this year so they are not re-argued next year.
Record the actions and owners in the reporting improvement plan.
checklist.done: a post-filing review is documented with dated actions to remove manual elements and lock in definitional decisions.

checklist.step: Retain the full filing evidence set
actions: File the submitted files, confirmations, attestation, mapping, tie-outs, validation reports and variance log under the data year and state.
Apply the 7-years-from-filing retention label and restrict edit access so the filed record cannot drift.
Confirm retrieval by state, line, data year and element for exam response.
Verify every state on the scoping matrix has a filed confirmation attached before the year's folder is closed.
checklist.done: the data year's MCAS evidence is filed, retention-labelled, edit-locked and complete against the scoping matrix.

testing.step: Rebuild the filing population from premium data
actions: Extract direct written premium by state, line and company from the Annual Statement state pages for the data year independently of Regulatory Reporting.
Apply the MCAS threshold and the participating-states list yourself and build your own list of required filings.
Compare your list to the scoping matrix and list every state-and-line the company scoped out but you scoped in.
Sign the population as complete with the premium source and extract date.
testing.done: an independently derived required-filing list is compared to the scoping matrix with every scoping difference listed.

testing.step: Confirm every required filing was actually submitted on time
actions: Open the MCAS application filing history and read status, submission timestamp and confirmation number for each state and line.
Compare each submission timestamp to the 30 April deadline and record days early or late.
Identify any refiling and read the stated restatement reason and the elements changed.
Flag any required filing with no submission record as an automatic exception.
testing.done: each required filing is traced to a submission record with its timestamp compared to the deadline and refilings identified.

testing.step: Draw the element sample
actions: Take 100% of elements that changed definition this data year and 100% of elements assembled manually.
Take 100% of elements driving the denial-rate, days-to-settle and complaint ratios given their examiner exposure.
Take 15 further element-and-state combinations at random (seeded, reproducible) across at least six states and three lines.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers changed and manual elements, ratio drivers and 15 random element-state combinations.

testing.step: Re-perform the element extraction from the frozen snapshot
actions: Read the element definition from the Data Call and Definitions and write your own query against the frozen snapshot without reading the production query first.
Compare your figure to the reported figure and investigate any difference over 0.5% to the specific records causing it.
Check the inclusion filter for the traps - cancelled and reinstated policies, reopened claims, duplicate complaint records, policies written by a different writing company in the same state.
Record your query, the reported figure, your figure and the reconciliation in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled element is independently re-extracted from the frozen snapshot and reconciled to the reported figure.

testing.step: Trace sampled elements to the systems of record
actions: Select ten underlying records per sampled element - individual claims, policies or complaints - and open each in its source system.
Confirm each record genuinely belongs in the reported element: right state, right line, right data-year dates, right disposition code.
Confirm ten records that were excluded were correctly excluded, so exclusion logic is tested as well as inclusion.
Attach the record-level evidence to the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled element has ten included and ten excluded records verified in the source system.

testing.step: Recompute the reported ratios and the median calculations
actions: Recompute claim denial rate, percentage closed without payment, complaint ratio and lawsuit rate from your re-extracted numerators and denominators.
Recompute median days to settle from the raw claim-level day counts rather than from a reported average, and confirm the day count runs from the definition's stated start event.
Compare each recomputed ratio to the filed value and list every difference with its cause.
Confirm outlier ratios were identified by the company before filing and carry an owned conduct review.
testing.done: every sampled ratio is recomputed from raw records and compared to the filed value, with outlier follow-up verified.

testing.step: Test the variance explanations
actions: Take every movement above the variance threshold and read the recorded explanation.
Test the explanation against independent evidence - a rate filing, a book transfer agreement, a system migration date, a claim-practice change memo.
Reject explanations that merely restate the movement, such as 'more claims were received'.
Log unsupported explanations as exceptions with the element and state affected.
testing.done: each material variance explanation is tested against independent evidence and unsupported ones are logged.

testing.step: Test attestation, review and segregation controls
actions: Confirm the attestation was signed by an officer with the authority required by the data call and dated before submission.
Confirm the business-owner confirmations exist for claims, complaints and policy elements and pre-date the attestation.
Confirm the preparer of an element is not the same person who reviewed and approved it.
Flag any submission made before the attestation date or reviewed by its own preparer.
testing.done: attestation authority, timing, business-owner confirmations and preparer-reviewer segregation are all verified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception recording state, line, element, the difference found and whether it changes a reported ratio.
Assign a root cause (definition misread, inclusion filter wrong, manual assembly error, snapshot taken before a late-posting batch, scoping threshold missed) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a filed figure is materially wrong, require a refiling decision from the Regulatory Reporting Manager with counsel input.
Carry every open issue into the next data year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue reference, root cause, owner, remediation date, refiling decision where needed, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate, the element tie-out pass rate and the count of ratio-affecting differences found.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references behind each figure.
Have an Internal Auditor who neither produced nor attested the submission sign the workpaper.
Report the result, the outlier ratio list and any refiling to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the on-time filing rate, tie-out pass rate, ratio differences, conclusion and committee reporting date.
