checklist.step: Maintain the metric catalogue with formulas and owners
actions: Hold each metric as a record with its formula, numerator and denominator definitions, source systems, cut basis, reporting dimensions (product, channel, state, target market) and named owner.
Align each metric definition to the MCAS element definition where an equivalent exists, so internal monitoring and regulatory reporting cannot diverge.
Retire or add metrics only through a change record stating the reason and the approver - a metric must never leave the pack silently.
Review the catalogue annually with the Chief Product Officer and the Complaints Manager.
checklist.done: every metric has a documented formula, source, dimension set and owner, with additions and retirements under a change record.

checklist.step: Set thresholds against published regulatory benchmarks
actions: Download the current published MCAS ratio distributions for each line and the NAIC Complaints Database Search results for the company and its peer group.
Set the amber threshold at the industry upper quartile and the red threshold at the industry 90th percentile for each ratio, or tighter where the internal customer-outcome standard is tighter.
Record the benchmark source, publication date and the exact percentile values used, so a threshold can be defended as evidence-based.
Re-approve thresholds annually with the Head of Compliance and document any threshold deliberately set looser than the benchmark with its rationale.
checklist.done: every metric carries amber and red thresholds tied to a dated, cited benchmark source and an approval record.

checklist.step: Refresh the underlying data and validate the load
actions: Run the quarter-end load of complaints, claims, policy, lapse, suitability and call-quality data into the conduct reporting layer.
Check row counts and control totals against each source system's own quarter-end report before the dashboard refreshes.
Fail the load rather than publish where a source is incomplete, and notify the metric owners the same day with the expected recovery time.
Record the load run id and validation results so every published metric points back to a specific run.
checklist.done: the quarter's conduct data load is validated against source control totals and published with a traceable run id.

checklist.step: Compute the complaint metrics and the external complaint index
actions: Compute complaints per 1,000 policies in force and complaints per 1,000 claims closed, split by product, channel and state, and separate DOI-forwarded complaints from direct ones.
Compute the average and worst acknowledgement and final-response times against each jurisdiction's deadline and report the percentage answered inside the deadline.
Pull the company's complaint index from the NAIC Complaints Database Search and compare it to the internally computed rate, explaining any gap in coverage or coding.
Break out the top five root-cause codes by volume and by quarter-on-quarter growth.
checklist.done: complaint rate, timeliness, external complaint index comparison and top root causes are computed and split by product, channel and state.

checklist.step: Compute the claims-outcome metrics
actions: Compute the claim denial rate, percentage closed without payment, median and 90th-percentile days to settle, and reopened-claim rate, split by product, cause of loss and channel.
Compute the lawsuit rate per 1,000 claims closed and the percentage of suits arising from denied claims.
Check denial-reason coding quality by sampling coded denials against the claim file narrative, since a denial rate is only as good as the reason codes behind it.
Deliver the metrics with the record counts behind every ratio so a reader can see thin denominators.
checklist.done: denial, timeliness, reopened and lawsuit metrics are computed with record counts and coding quality checked.

checklist.step: Compute the sales-practice and suitability metrics
actions: Compute the suitability review declination rate, the override rate and the override-to-sale conversion rate by producer and by agency.
Compute replacement rate, external-versus-internal replacement split, free-look cancellation rate and first-year and 13-month lapse and surrender rates.
Rank producers by a composite outlier score across replacement, lapse and override rates and hand the top decile to Distribution Compliance for file review.
Split every metric by target market segment so a product sold outside its intended market becomes visible.
checklist.done: suitability, replacement, free-look and early-lapse metrics are computed by producer, agency and target-market segment.

checklist.step: Compute the servicing and call-quality metrics
actions: Compute first-contact resolution, abandonment rate, average speed of answer and the volume of calls escalated to a complaint.
Pull the QA scoring results for disclosure delivery, vulnerable-customer handling and complaint identification, and report the pass rate and the failure themes.
Report the percentage of calls where a complaint indicator was raised by the QA reviewer but not logged as a complaint by the agent, since that gap suppresses every complaint metric.
Deliver the results to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager with the sampled call references.
checklist.done: servicing and QA metrics are computed, including the unlogged-complaint gap with sampled call references.

checklist.step: Run the post-launch product oversight review on the metrics
actions: For each product launched or materially changed in the last 24 months, read its conduct metrics against the target-market outcomes stated in the product approval paper.
Test the specific expectations recorded at launch - expected persistency, expected claim acceptance rate, expected complaint volume - and state whether each held.
Where outcomes diverge, decide and record the action: distribution restriction, disclosure change, repricing, target-market redefinition or withdrawal from sale.
Present the review to the Product Governance Forum with the metric evidence attached.
checklist.done: every product in its first 24 months has a documented post-launch review comparing actual outcomes to the target-market expectations set at approval.

checklist.step: Compare every metric to its threshold and colour the pack
actions: Apply the approved amber and red thresholds to every metric at every reporting dimension, not only at the total company level, since a state-level breach hides inside a healthy total.
Flag any metric amber for two consecutive quarters as a trend breach even where it never reaches red.
Produce the exception list with metric, dimension, value, threshold, direction of travel and owner.
Publish the dashboard within 15 business days of quarter end and notify each breaching metric's owner directly.
checklist.done: thresholds are applied at every dimension, trend breaches are flagged, and each breach owner is notified within 15 business days.

checklist.step: Drill into every red breach to a root cause
actions: For each red breach, pull the underlying records - the actual complaints, denied claims or lapsed policies - and read at least 20 of them.
Determine whether the driver is a process defect, a producer or agency concentration, a product design issue, a system defect or a coding artefact.
State the customer impact in numbers: how many customers, what detriment, whether redress is owed.
Write the root-cause note with the evidence references and hand it to the accountable business owner.
checklist.done: every red breach has a file-level root-cause note stating the driver, the number of customers affected and whether redress is owed.

checklist.step: Open and track remediation for every breach
actions: Raise a GRC issue per red breach and per two-quarter amber trend with the root cause, owner, action and completion date.
Where customer detriment is identified, open a redress workstream with a defined population, a redress calculation basis and a completion date.
Require the metric itself, not just the action, to be the closure test - the issue closes when the metric returns inside threshold for two quarters.
Report ageing issues to the Conduct Risk Committee each quarter.
checklist.done: every breach has a tracked issue whose closure test is the metric returning inside threshold for two quarters.

checklist.step: Feed conduct findings back into distribution and training
actions: Take the outlier producer and agency list and open a file review of at least ten sales per outlier, covering suitability documentation and disclosure delivery.
Apply the graduated response recorded in the distribution compliance policy - coaching, supervision plan, commission hold, contract termination - and record which was applied and why.
Assign targeted training through the LMS to the producers and agencies driving the metric.
Re-measure the outliers the following quarter and report whether the intervention moved the metric.
checklist.done: each outlier producer or agency has a file review, a graduated response, targeted training and a next-quarter re-measurement.

checklist.step: Present the pack and take decisions at committee
actions: Present the quarterly pack to the Conduct Risk Committee within 25 business days of quarter end with the breach list at the front, not in an appendix.
Ask the committee for explicit decisions on products and channels sitting outside expectation, and minute the decision and its owner.
Escalate to the Board Risk Committee any breach involving systemic customer detriment or a metric in the industry 90th percentile for two consecutive quarters.
Record accepted risks with an expiry date so acceptance cannot become permanent.
checklist.done: the pack is presented within 25 business days with minuted decisions, named owners and dated risk acceptances.

checklist.step: Reconcile the internal metrics to what is reported externally
actions: Reconcile the quarterly internal complaint, denial and timeliness metrics to the figures filed in MCAS for the overlapping period.
Investigate and document any difference caused by definition, cut basis or scope, and confirm neither figure is wrong.
Where the internal metric is more adverse than the filed figure, confirm the filed figure is still correct under the data-call definition.
Record the reconciliation in the quarterly pack as evidence that internal and regulatory views agree.
checklist.done: internal conduct metrics reconcile to the filed MCAS figures with every definitional difference documented.

checklist.step: Retain the pack and its underlying data
actions: File the pack, the metric extracts, threshold approvals, root-cause notes and committee minutes under the quarter.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the reporting quarter.
Confirm the metric values as reported can be reproduced later by storing the load run id and the extract alongside the pack.
Verify every breach in the pack links to its GRC issue before the quarter's folder is closed.
checklist.done: the quarter's pack, extracts, run id and minutes are filed, retention-labelled, and every breach links to an issue.

testing.step: Extract the metric catalogue and the quarter's reported values
actions: Export the approved metric catalogue with formulas, thresholds, dimensions and owners as at quarter end.
Export the quarter's published metric values at every dimension from the dashboard.
Compare the catalogue to the pack and list any metric in the catalogue that did not appear in the pack, and any pack metric absent from the catalogue.
Sign the population as complete with extract dates and counts.
testing.done: catalogue and reported values are extracted and compared, with every missing or unapproved metric listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the reporting layer to the source systems
actions: Take complaint, claim, policy and lapse record counts from the conduct reporting layer for the quarter.
Compare each to the source system's own quarter-end report and to the general ledger where a financial total exists.
Investigate any difference over 1% to the specific records and determine whether records were dropped by a load filter.
Document the reconciliation and any load defect in the workpaper.
testing.done: reporting-layer record counts reconcile to source systems within 1% or every difference is traced to specific records.

testing.step: Draw the metric sample
actions: Take 100% of metrics in red breach and 100% of metrics whose definition or threshold changed in the quarter.
Take 100% of metrics that moved more than one threshold band since the prior quarter.
Take 10 further metrics at random (seeded, reproducible) across complaints, claims, suitability and servicing.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all red, changed and band-moving metrics plus 10 random metrics across the four domains.

testing.step: Recompute sampled metrics from raw records
actions: Read the catalogue formula and build your own numerator and denominator from the raw record extracts without using the dashboard measure.
Confirm the denominator basis matches the definition - policies in force at quarter end versus average in force changes a complaint rate materially.
Compare your value to the published value at total and at two lower dimensions, and reconcile any difference over 1%.
Record both values and the reconciliation in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled metric is independently recomputed at total and two lower dimensions and reconciled to the published value.

testing.step: Verify the benchmarks and thresholds against their published source
actions: Open the cited MCAS ratio distribution and the NAIC complaint index source and read the percentile values yourself.
Compare them to the thresholds recorded in the catalogue and flag any threshold not supported by the cited source or based on a superseded publication.
Confirm any threshold set looser than the benchmark carries a documented rationale and an approval.
Capture the benchmark source page into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled threshold traces to a current published benchmark value or is logged as unsupported.

testing.step: Test the underlying data quality behind the metrics
actions: Select 25 claims coded as denied and read the file narrative to confirm the denial coding is right, since miscoding moves the denial rate both ways.
Select 25 customer contacts flagged by QA as complaint-indicative and confirm each was logged in the complaints register.
Select 25 suitability overrides and confirm the recorded override reason matches the documentation on the file.
Quantify the coding error rate and restate the affected metric to show the impact.
testing.done: denial coding, complaint logging and override reasons are file-tested with the coding error rate quantified and metrics restated.

testing.step: Test that breaches were detected and escalated on time
actions: Apply the thresholds yourself to the published values at every dimension and build your own breach list.
Compare to the breaches reported in the pack and list any breach the pack missed, especially at state or channel level.
Recompute the days between data availability and the escalation date for each red breach and compare to the 5-business-day requirement.
Confirm every breach has a GRC issue with a named owner and a metric-based closure test.
testing.done: an independently derived breach list is compared to the reported one, with escalation timing recomputed against the 5-day rule.

testing.step: Test the remediation actually moved the metric
actions: Take breaches closed in the quarter and read the closure evidence.
Confirm the metric returned inside threshold for two consecutive quarters rather than the issue being closed on action completion alone.
For breaches involving customer detriment, confirm the redress population, calculation basis and payment evidence exist.
Reopen in the workpaper any issue closed without the metric evidence and log it as an exception.
testing.done: each closed breach is tested against the two-quarter metric-return standard and any redress is traced to payment evidence.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception recording the metric, dimension, the defect and whether it understated conduct risk.
Assign a root cause (formula error, denominator basis wrong, load filter dropping records, coding quality, threshold not refreshed, breach not escalated) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and require restatement of any published metric found materially wrong, with a note to the committee that received it.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue reference, root cause, owner, remediation date, restatement where needed, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the metric recomputation pass rate, the count of missed breaches and the average escalation delay in business days.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references behind each figure.
Have an Internal Auditor who built no dashboard and owns no breaching metric sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any restated metric to the Conduct Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the recomputation pass rate, missed breaches, escalation delay, conclusion and committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the standing exam-readiness file so any supervisor's standardised data request can be answered from an existing, current evidence set rather than a scramble

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - IAIS ICP 22 (AML/CFT), Standard 22.3 on the risk-based approach and ICP 9 (Supervisory Review and Reporting) on the insurer's duty to make information available to the supervisor, operationalised through the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook examination standards and the standardised data request formats used by state examiners

In-scope processes.value: Continuous maintenance of the exam file across every Market Regulation Handbook review area - company operations and management, complaint handling, marketing and sales, producer licensing, policyholder service, underwriting and rating, and claims - for every state the company is licensed in

In-scope systems.value: Exam readiness library in the compliance evidence repository, with source data extracts standing ready from the policy administration, claims and complaints systems and a secure transfer channel for examiner delivery

Compliance procedure documented.value: Market Conduct Exam Readiness Procedure - the standing file index by review area, the refresh cadence per artefact, data-request extract specifications, the exam intake and coordination protocol, privilege review and the secure delivery route

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with Regulatory Counsel concurrence on the privilege and confidentiality steps; reviewed annually and after every completed exam

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: File refreshed quarterly with the current quarter's data and monthly for complaint and claim registers; once an exam call letter arrives, the initial data request is typically due within 30 days and subsequent examiner requests within 10 business days each

Deadline reminders configured.value: Quarterly refresh tasks per review area with owner reminders at 15 and 5 days before due; on an active exam, every examiner request logged with its due date and alerts at 5, 3 and 1 days out

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Exam files, delivered data extracts with their record counts, examiner correspondence and the final report retained 10 years from exam close, and readiness refresh evidence 7 years from the refresh date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Stale artefacts past their refresh date, review areas with no owner, extracts that cannot reproduce a prior delivered figure, and any late or incomplete examiner response are logged with an owner and a correction date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off the quarterly readiness attestation and the closure of every stale-artefact or failed-extract exception

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The full exam-readiness index - every required artefact across all Market Regulation Handbook review areas - plus every examiner request received and answered in the tested period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of index artefacts present and inside their refresh window; every standard data request extract must run and reconcile to source within 1%; any examiner request answered late or incompletely is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; test runs quarterly over the index and, where an exam was active, over 100% of that exam's requests and deliveries

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not maintain the exam file or have prepared any tested data delivery, and runs at least one unannounced readiness drill per year

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly Exam Readiness test workpaper (index completeness check, drill results, extract re-performance, request timeliness analysis) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The exam file itself - procedures, org charts, registers, data extracts and prior exam findings - producible within the examiner's stated deadline, with a delivery log recording what was sent, when and to whom

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager is the single exam coordinator and sole channel to the examiner; Regulatory Counsel reviews every delivery for privilege and confidentiality before it leaves

checklist.step: Build the exam file index from the examination standards
actions: Take the Market Regulation Handbook review areas - company operations and management, complaint handling, marketing and sales, producer licensing, policyholder service, underwriting and rating, claims - and create a folder per area.

Under each area list the artefacts examiners routinely request: current procedures, org charts and delegated authorities, the complaint register, advertising log and approvals, producer appointment and termination registers, underwriting guidelines and rate manuals in force by period, claims manuals, and the prior exam report with its corrective actions.
Set a refresh cadence per artefact - monthly for the complaint and claim registers, quarterly for procedures and registers, on-change for guidelines and manuals.
Name an owner per artefact and record it in the index.
checklist.done: an index exists covering every review area, listing each artefact with an owner and a refresh cadence.

checklist.step: Pre-build the standardised data request extracts
actions: Write and save a standing extract per standard examiner data request: policies issued, policies declined or non-renewed, cancellations, claims paid, claims denied, claims closed without payment, complaints, and producer terminations, each keyed by state and period.
Match every field to the examiner's usual layout - policy number, insured name, state, effective and expiry dates, transaction dates, disposition, reason code and premium or paid amount.
Parameterise the extracts by state and date range so a request can be run the day it arrives rather than built from scratch.
Store the query text, expected record counts and last successful run date with the extract definition.
checklist.done: each standard examiner data request has a saved, parameterised extract with stored query text and a last-run date.

checklist.step: Refresh the registers on their monthly cadence
actions: Each month refresh the complaint register, the claims register extract, the advertising approval log and the producer appointment and termination register into the exam file.
Reconcile each refreshed register to its source system count and record the count in the file so a later examiner figure can be defended.
Verify every register carries the fields examiners ask for, including complaint receipt and closure dates, DOI file numbers and root-cause codes.
Mark the refresh date on the index and clear the reminder task.
checklist.done: every monthly register is refreshed, count-reconciled to source, and date-stamped on the index.

checklist.step: Keep point-in-time underwriting and rating evidence retrievable
actions: Archive each version of underwriting guidelines, rate manuals, rating rules and policy forms with its effective-from and effective-to date, by state and writing company.
Link each archived version to its SERFF filing and approval so the examiner can see the filed and approved basis for the rates in force.
Test retrieval by asking for the rate manual in force in a named state on a stated past date and confirming exactly one version returns.
Record any period where the version in force cannot be identified as a readiness gap with an owner.
checklist.done: the rate, rule and form version in force in any state on any past date is uniquely retrievable and linked to its filing.

checklist.step: Maintain the company operations and governance pack
actions: Keep current the org charts, the compliance function structure and reporting lines, the delegated authority matrix and the outsourcing and third-party administrator register with each contract's oversight terms.
Keep the licence and certificate-of-authority schedule by state and writing company, with lines of authority.
Keep the record-retention schedule and the disaster-recovery evidence examiners ask for under company operations.
Refresh quarterly and after any reorganisation or new outsourcing arrangement.
checklist.done: org, delegated authority, outsourcing, licence and retention artefacts are current within the quarter and refreshed after any structural change.

checklist.step: Keep the prior exam findings and their evidence at the front of the file
actions: Hold the last three exam reports for every state with the corrective action plan, the completion evidence and any restitution records.
Record for each finding the current status and the evidence that the fix is still operating today, not merely that it was implemented once.
Flag any prior finding whose control has since degraded, since an examiner returning to a repeat finding is the worst exam outcome.
Review the set quarterly with the owning functions.
checklist.done: every prior exam finding carries current operating evidence and any degraded control is flagged for repair.

checklist.step: Run a quarterly readiness self-check
actions: Check every index artefact for presence, refresh date inside its cadence and a live owner.
Run every standing extract end to end and confirm it completes, returns plausible counts and reconciles to source within 1%.
List stale, missing, ownerless or failing items with an owner and a correction date.
Report the readiness percentage by review area to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: a quarterly self-check reports readiness by review area with every stale, missing or failing item owned and dated.

checklist.step: Rehearse with an unannounced drill
actions: At least annually issue a simulated examiner data request without notice, using a real standardised data request format and a real state and period.
Measure elapsed time to a complete, reconciled response and record where it stalled - missing owner, extract failure, data that only exists in an archived system.
Test one point-in-time question deliberately, such as the underwriting guideline in force in a named state 30 months ago.
Debrief with the exam coordinator and convert every stall into a dated fix.
checklist.done: an unannounced drill is completed with elapsed time measured and every stall converted into a dated fix.

checklist.step: Run the exam intake protocol when a call letter arrives
actions: Log the call letter with the state, exam type (comprehensive or targeted), exam period, review areas and the initial data request due date, commonly 30 days.
Name the exam coordinator as the single channel to the examiner and instruct all staff that no data, document or explanation goes to the examiner except through that channel.
Stand up the response team with a named owner per review area and hold a kick-off within three business days.
Notify Regulatory Counsel, the Head of Compliance and the affected business heads with the deadline calendar.
checklist.done: the exam is logged with its period and deadlines, a single coordinator channel is enforced, and area owners are named within three business days.

checklist.step: Produce the initial data request from the standing extracts
actions: Map each examiner request line to the standing extract that answers it and note where a new extract is genuinely required.
Run each extract for the exam state and period, and record run id, record count and run date.
Reconcile the record counts to the systems of record and to any figure previously filed in MCAS for the same period, and explain any difference before delivery.
Hand the reconciled extracts to the exam coordinator with the reconciliation notes attached.
checklist.done: every request line is answered by a run, count-reconciled extract with its reconciliation note attached.

checklist.step: Review every delivery for privilege, confidentiality and accuracy
actions: Read each document set before delivery and withhold privileged legal advice, applying the state's confidentiality and privilege protections and logging what was withheld and why.
Redact non-responsive personal data of uninvolved third parties in line with the privacy standard.
Confirm the response actually answers the question asked and does not volunteer material outside the request.
Approve the delivery in writing before it is sent.
checklist.done: each delivery carries a written counsel approval, a privilege log for anything withheld, and redactions applied where required.

checklist.step: Deliver through the agreed secure channel and log it
actions: Send through the examiner's designated secure portal or encrypted transfer, never by unencrypted email.
Log each delivery with request id, date sent, file names, record counts, the extract run ids and the recipient examiner.
Keep a byte-identical copy of exactly what was delivered so a later question about a figure can be answered from the same file.
Confirm receipt with the examiner and record the confirmation.
checklist.done: every delivery is sent securely, logged with run ids and counts, copied verbatim, and receipt-confirmed.

checklist.step: Track examiner requests, interviews and criticisms during the exam
actions: Log every subsequent examiner request with its due date, usually 10 business days, and an owner.
Prepare each interviewee with the relevant procedure and file evidence, and have a second Compliance attendee take notes at every examiner interview.
Log every criticism or preliminary finding the examiner raises, with the underlying file references, and respond with evidence inside the stated window.
Escalate any request the business cannot meet in time to the coordinator before the deadline, never after.
checklist.done: every examiner request, interview and criticism is logged with an owner, a deadline and a documented, evidenced response.

checklist.step: Close the exam and fold the lessons back into the file
actions: Review the draft report, prepare the company response to each finding within the state's response window and record where the company disagrees with reasons and evidence.
File the final adopted report, the response and any order in the exam file and hand each finding to remediation tracking.
Update the exam file index with any artefact the examiner asked for that the file did not hold, so it is standing ready next time.
Debrief the response team and record what slowed the exam.
checklist.done: the adopted report and company response are filed, findings are handed to remediation, and every missing artefact is added to the index.

checklist.step: Retain the exam record under its longer retention
actions: File the call letter, all requests, all delivered files, correspondence, interview notes, the draft and final reports and the company response under the exam.
Apply the 10-years-from-exam-close retention label, longer than the standard evidence rule, since repeat-finding analysis reaches back across exam cycles.
Confirm retrieval by state, exam period and review area.
Verify every logged delivery has its verbatim copy attached before the exam folder is locked.
checklist.done: the complete exam record is filed under a 10-year label, indexed by state and period, with every delivery copy attached.

testing.step: Extract the readiness index as the population
actions: Export the exam file index with every artefact, review area, owner, cadence and last refresh date.
Compare the index to the Market Regulation Handbook review-area list and list any review area with thin or no coverage.
Add every examiner request received in the period as a second population.
Sign both populations as complete with counts and extract date.
testing.done: the index is extracted, compared to the handbook review areas, and combined with the period's examiner requests as a signed population.

testing.step: Test index completeness and staleness
actions: For each index artefact confirm the document or extract actually exists in the repository, not merely a placeholder row.
Recompute days since last refresh against each artefact's stated cadence and list every stale item with days overdue.
Confirm each owner is a current employee in the stated role using the HRIS org data.
List artefacts with no owner, no file or an overdue refresh as exceptions.
testing.done: every index row is verified for file existence, refresh currency and a live owner, with staleness quantified in days.

testing.step: Draw the sample across review areas and requests
actions: Take 100% of examiner requests answered in the period and 100% of standing extracts that failed the quarterly self-check.
Take two artefacts from each Market Regulation Handbook review area at random (seeded, reproducible).
Include at least three point-in-time retrieval tests spanning periods over 24 months old.
Record the seed, population sizes, strata and selection date.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all examiner requests, failed extracts, two artefacts per review area and three point-in-time retrievals.

testing.step: Re-run the standing extracts and reconcile to source
actions: Run each sampled standing extract for a named state and period and confirm it completes without manual intervention.
Reconcile the record count to the source system for the same state and period and investigate any difference over 1%.
Confirm the field layout still matches the examiner's expected format, including reason codes and disposition values.
Record run time, counts and reconciliation in the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled extract runs unaided, matches the expected layout and reconciles to source within 1% or the difference is traced.

testing.step: Run an unannounced retrieval drill
actions: Issue a live request without notice for a named state and a period over two years old, in a real standardised data request format.
Time the response from request to complete, reconciled delivery and record every point where it stalled.
Include a point-in-time question - the underwriting guideline, rate manual and complaint procedure in force on a stated past date - and confirm exactly one version returns for each.
Compare the elapsed time to the 30-day initial request and 10-business-day follow-up standards.
testing.done: an unannounced drill produces a measured elapsed time against the 30-day and 10-day standards with every stall documented.

testing.step: Test the fidelity of what was actually delivered
actions: For each sampled examiner request, open the retained verbatim copy of the delivery and the delivery log entry.
Re-run the recorded extract run id and confirm it reproduces the delivered figures exactly.
Confirm counts stated in the cover response match the file contents, and that every request line was answered rather than partially addressed.
Flag any delivery that cannot be reproduced or that answered fewer lines than requested.
testing.done: each sampled delivery is reproducible from its run id and answers every request line, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Recompute request response timeliness
actions: For each examiner request recompute business days between the request date and the delivery date.
Compare to the stated deadline - 30 days for the initial data request, 10 business days for follow-ups, or the examiner's stated date where different.
Confirm any extension was requested before the deadline and granted in writing by the examiner.
Log every late delivery with days late and whether an extension was in place.
testing.done: response times are recomputed against each stated deadline with every late delivery and unapproved extension logged.

testing.step: Test privilege review and channel discipline
actions: Confirm a written counsel approval pre-dates each sampled delivery and that a privilege log exists for anything withheld.
Check the delivery log and mailbox records for any material sent to the examiner outside the coordinator channel.
Review two deliveries for over-disclosure - material provided beyond the request that creates unnecessary exposure - and for personal data that should have been redacted.
Record findings on channel discipline and disclosure scope.
testing.done: counsel approval, privilege logging, single-channel discipline and redaction are verified across the sampled deliveries.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception recording the review area, artefact or request, the defect and the exam exposure it creates.
Assign a root cause (owner vacancy, cadence never run, archived system unreachable, extract broken by a schema change, delivery outside channel) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and require re-drill of any area that failed the retrieval test.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's readiness test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue reference, root cause, owner, remediation date and a re-drill or retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute readiness percentage by review area, drill elapsed time, extract pass rate and the count of late examiner responses.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references behind each figure.
Have an Internal Auditor who maintains no part of the exam file and prepared no tested delivery sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any review area below the readiness standard to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states readiness by review area, drill time, extract pass rate, conclusion and committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the corrective action plan for every adopted exam finding and the evidence that each fix is operating before the agreed date

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - IAIS ICP 22 (AML/CFT), Standard 22.3 on risk-proportionate measures and ICP 9 (Supervisory Review and Reporting) on responding to supervisory findings, implemented through each state's examination statute requiring a corrective action plan after the adopted report and through the terms of any consent order or stipulation

In-scope processes.value: Remediation of every criticism, recommendation, finding and order arising from a market conduct or financial exam, an AML independent test or a supervisory review - from adopted report through root-cause fix, customer restitution and validation of sustained operation

In-scope systems.value: Findings, corrective actions, owners, dates and evidence tracked in the GRC platform, with restitution populations and payments evidenced from the policy administration and claims platforms

Compliance procedure documented.value: Exam Finding Remediation Procedure - finding intake and decomposition, root-cause analysis, corrective action design, restitution scoping and payment, evidence standards for closure, extension approval and regulator status reporting

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with Regulatory Counsel concurrence on the regulator communication and consent-order steps; reviewed annually and after every exam close

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Company response to the draft report inside the state's stated window, commonly 30 days from receipt; corrective action plan filed within 30 days of the adopted report; each action completed by the date agreed with the regulator, and any consent-order milestone and restitution deadline tracked to its ordered date

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC alerts to each action owner at 30, 14 and 7 days before the agreed date, daily inside 7 days, and automatic escalation to the Head of Compliance on the first day an action passes its date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Adopted report, corrective action plan, evidence of each fix, restitution population and payment files, regulator correspondence and closure confirmations retained 10 years from exam close

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missed action dates, closures without evidence, restitution populations that later expand, and repeat findings from a prior exam are each logged with cause, regulator notification decision and a revised date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs closure of every finding after validation evidence is in hand, and approves any request to the regulator for an extended date

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every open and closed exam finding across all states for the period, with their corrective actions, agreed dates, restitution populations and closure evidence

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero findings closed without validation evidence and zero actions passing their agreed date without a regulator-approved extension; any repeat of a prior-exam finding is an automatic fail and a Board-level escalation

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Validation is owned by Internal Audit independent of Compliance, and the Chief Audit Executive signs the validation conclusion for consent-order findings

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly Exam Remediation test workpaper (finding population, action tracing, restitution recalculation, closure evidence review, exception schedule) in the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Corrective action plan with status per finding, evidence packs per closed action, restitution reconciliation and the regulator status letters, producible for a re-exam or order compliance check within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager sends all status reporting to the DOI through the exam coordinator channel; Regulatory Counsel drafts and clears every extension request, consent-order response and restitution communication

checklist.step: Take in the adopted report and decompose it into discrete findings
actions: Read the adopted report and create one GRC finding record per criticism, recommendation and ordered action, never one record per report section.
Capture on each record the state, exam period, review area, the standard breached, the examiner's stated error rate or sample result, and whether it is a criticism, a recommendation or an order term.
Attach the report extract and the underlying examiner workpaper reference to each record.
Flag any finding that repeats a finding from a prior exam of the same state or a different state.
checklist.done: each criticism, recommendation and order term is a separate finding record with the standard breached, examiner evidence and a repeat flag.

checklist.step: Agree the response and the completion dates with the regulator
actions: Draft the company response per finding inside the state's response window, commonly 30 days, stating agreement, partial agreement with reasons and evidence, or disagreement with the basis.
Propose a completion date per finding that the owning function has actually committed to, not an optimistic date to please the examiner.
File the corrective action plan within 30 days of the adopted report and record the state's acceptance or amendment of the dates.
Write the accepted date onto each GRC finding record as the agreed date, distinct from any internal target.
checklist.done: the corrective action plan is filed within 30 days with a regulator-accepted completion date recorded on every finding.

checklist.step: Establish the true root cause before designing a fix
actions: For each finding, pull the examiner's failed sample files plus a further 25 files from the same population and read them.
Determine whether the driver is a procedure defect, a system configuration or logic error, a training gap, a capacity or throughput problem, or a third-party administrator failure.
Test whether the same driver exists in other states, other products or other channels that the examiner did not review - the finding is rarely confined to the exam scope.
Write the root-cause statement with the file evidence and the scope of contamination for each finding.
checklist.done: each finding has an evidenced root-cause statement and a stated scope covering states, products and channels beyond the exam.

checklist.step: Design corrective actions that address the cause, not the symptom
actions: For each finding define the actions: procedure change, system change, control addition, training, staffing, third-party contract change - with a named owner and date each.
Reject any action that is only 'reminder communication issued' or 'staff reminded' where the root cause was a system or procedure defect.
Define the closure evidence for each action up front - the approved procedure version, the release ticket, the control test result, the training completion report.
Have the accountable business head confirm the actions and dates in writing before the plan goes to the regulator.
checklist.done: every finding has actions with owners, dates, pre-agreed closure evidence and a written business-head commitment.

checklist.step: Scope and quantify the affected customer population
actions: Build the affected population from the root-cause criteria across the full contamination scope, not just the exam state and period.
Reconcile the population count to the source systems and document the inclusion and exclusion logic in writing.
Split the population into customers who suffered financial detriment, non-financial detriment and no detriment, with the test applied to each.
Hand the population and its reconciliation to the restitution owner and to Regulatory Counsel.
checklist.done: the affected population is built across the full contamination scope, reconciled to source, and split by detriment type.

checklist.step: Calculate and pay restitution where customers were harmed
actions: Agree the restitution basis with Regulatory Counsel and the regulator where the order specifies it - underpaid claim amount, overcharged premium, plus statutory interest at the state's rate from the date of detriment.
Compute the amount per customer, have it independently recalculated on a sample before any payment run, and post the total to a restitution liability account.
Issue payments with the explanatory letter cleared by counsel, and track uncashed cheques through to escheatment where required.
Reconcile payments issued to the affected population and report the completion percentage weekly until it closes.
checklist.done: restitution is computed with interest, independently recalculated on a sample, paid, and reconciled to the affected population.

checklist.step: Implement the system and procedure fixes under change control
actions: Raise a change record per system fix, linked to the GRC finding id so the regulatory driver is visible in the change queue.
Specify the acceptance test that proves the defect is gone - for example that the rating engine now applies the filed factor, or that the claim workflow blocks closure without the required notice.
Execute the test in a non-production environment, capture the result, and deploy with the release evidence attached to the finding record.
Confirm post-deployment in production with a live transaction rather than assuming the release worked.
checklist.done: each system fix has a linked change record, a passed acceptance test, release evidence and a production confirmation.

checklist.step: Retrain and re-communicate to the population that failed
actions: Build the training to the specific failure - the actual disclosure that was missed, the actual notice deadline that was blown - not a general refresher.
Assign it to the exact population that performs the process, drawn from the HRIS role data, with a completion date before the finding's agreed date.
Include a short assessment so completion means comprehension, and require managers to review failures with their staff.
Report completion to the finding owner as closure evidence.
checklist.done: targeted training is assigned to the performing population, completed with assessment before the agreed date, and reported as evidence.

checklist.step: Track every action against its agreed date and escalate slippage early
actions: Review the open action list weekly with owners and record percentage complete against the plan, not against a re-baselined date.
Escalate any action that will miss its agreed date to the Head of Compliance at least 30 days before that date, so an extension can be requested before the breach.
Never quietly move an agreed date in the tracker - a change to a regulator-agreed date requires a regulator-approved extension.
Report the ageing profile of open actions monthly to the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: open actions are reviewed weekly against original agreed dates with slippage escalated at least 30 days before the date.

checklist.step: Request any extension from the regulator before the date passes
actions: Draft the extension request stating what is complete, what is outstanding, why the date cannot be met and the new proposed date with the basis for confidence in it.
Send through the exam coordinator channel before the original date, never after, and record the submission date.
Record the regulator's response and, on approval, update the agreed date on the finding record with the approval attached.
Where an extension is refused, escalate immediately to the Head of Compliance and the accountable executive for resourcing.
checklist.done: every date change is supported by an extension requested before the original date and an attached regulator approval.

checklist.step: Validate that each fix actually works before claiming closure
actions: For each action proposed for closure, test a fresh sample of transactions processed after the fix date - a minimum of 25 items or the full population if smaller.
Confirm the defect the examiner found does not recur in that sample and that the promised evidence artefact exists.
Reject closure where the evidence is an assertion, a project status slide or a completed task with no output.
Write the validation note with the sample, the result and the conclusion, and return failed actions to the owner with a new date.
checklist.done: each closed action carries an independent validation note testing post-fix transactions, with failed validations returned to the owner.

checklist.step: Sweep the contamination scope outside the exam state
actions: For each finding, run the same test in the other states, products and channels identified in the root-cause scope.
Where the defect exists elsewhere, extend the corrective action and the restitution population rather than waiting for another state to find it.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel whether a proactive notification to other states is required or advisable, and record the decision and its rationale.
Record the sweep result on the finding record even where nothing further was found.
checklist.done: each finding has a documented sweep result across other states, products and channels, with any extension of scope actioned.

checklist.step: Report remediation status to the regulator and to governance
actions: Send the regulator the status report on the cadence the order or exam letter requires, listing each finding, its action, status, evidence and completion date.
Report to the Compliance Committee monthly and to the Board Risk Committee quarterly on open findings, actions past their agreed date, restitution completion and any repeat finding.
Escalate any repeat of a prior-exam finding to the Board with a named executive accountable, since repeat findings drive penalties and orders.
Minute every decision to accept a delay with its rationale and expiry.
checklist.done: regulator status reporting is sent on its required cadence and governance receives monthly and quarterly reporting including repeat findings.

checklist.step: Confirm closure with the regulator and prepare for re-examination
actions: Submit the closure package per finding with the validation evidence and, where restitution applied, the payment reconciliation.
Obtain and file the regulator's written acknowledgement or release, and treat a finding as open until that acknowledgement arrives.
Add each finding, its fix and its validation evidence to the exam readiness file so a re-examination can be answered from the standing file.
Schedule a re-test of each fixed control 12 months after closure to prove it is still operating.
checklist.done: each finding has a submitted closure package, a filed regulator acknowledgement, exam-file evidence and a 12-month re-test scheduled.

checklist.step: Retain the remediation record
actions: File the adopted report, corrective action plan, action evidence, validation notes, restitution files and all regulator correspondence under the exam and finding id.
Apply the 10-years-from-exam-close retention label so repeat-finding analysis spans exam cycles.
Confirm retrieval by state, exam period, finding id and review area.
Verify every closed finding links to its validation note and regulator acknowledgement before the folder is locked.
checklist.done: the remediation record is filed under a 10-year label and every closed finding links to validation and regulator acknowledgement.

testing.step: Build the finding population from the source reports
actions: Export every exam finding record open or closed in the period with state, exam, agreed date, status, owner and closure date.
Read the adopted exam reports and consent orders themselves and count the criticisms, recommendations and order terms independently.
Compare your count to the tracked records and list any finding in a report that never became a tracked record.
Sign the population as complete with the reports relied on.
testing.done: the tracked finding population is reconciled to the adopted reports themselves with every untracked finding listed.

testing.step: Reconcile agreed dates to the regulator's own correspondence
actions: For each finding, open the filed corrective action plan and the regulator's acceptance letter and read the agreed completion date.
Compare it to the agreed date held in the tracker and flag any tracker date later than the regulator-accepted date.
Where a later date exists, confirm an extension request was sent before the original date and approved in writing.
List every silently re-baselined date as an exception.
testing.done: every tracked agreed date is traced to regulator correspondence with silently re-baselined dates listed.

testing.step: Draw the sample of findings and actions
actions: Take 100% of consent-order terms, 100% of findings involving restitution and 100% of repeat findings.
Take 100% of actions closed in the quarter where the closure evidence was training or communication only.
Take 15 further actions at random (seeded, reproducible) across states and review areas.
Record the seed, population sizes, strata and selection date.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all order terms, restitution and repeat findings, all soft closures and 15 random actions.

testing.step: Re-perform the closure validation on post-fix transactions
actions: For each sampled closed action, draw your own sample of 25 transactions processed after the recorded fix date.
Test for the specific defect the examiner identified - the missing notice, the wrong rate factor, the late claim acknowledgement - without reading the company's validation note first.
Compare your result to the recorded validation conclusion and treat any recurrence as a failed closure, not a residual issue.
Capture the transaction evidence into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled closure is independently re-tested on post-fix transactions with any recurrence recorded as a failed closure.

testing.step: Test the quality of the closure evidence itself
actions: Open the evidence attached to each sampled closed action and confirm it is the artefact the plan promised - approved procedure version, release ticket with test result, control test output, training completion report.
Reject status slides, meeting minutes and email assertions as closure evidence and log them as exceptions.
Confirm the evidence date falls before the closure date and after the finding date.
Confirm the evidence covers the full contamination scope, not only the exam state.
testing.done: closure evidence is verified as the promised artefact, correctly dated, and covering the full scope, with assertions logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Recompute the restitution population and amounts
actions: Rebuild the affected population yourself from the root-cause criteria and compare your count to the company's population.
Recompute restitution for 25 customers including statutory interest from the detriment date at the state's stated rate.
Reconcile total payments issued to the restitution liability account and to bank clearing, and check the treatment of uncashed cheques and escheatment.
Flag any customer in your population who received nothing.
testing.done: the restitution population and amounts are independently rebuilt and recomputed, and payments reconcile to the liability and bank records.

testing.step: Recompute action timeliness against agreed dates
actions: For each sampled action compute days between the regulator-accepted date and the actual completion date.
Count actions completed late, actions still open past their date, and actions closed on time but later failing validation.
Confirm the corrective action plan itself was filed within 30 days of the adopted report and the company response inside the state's response window.
Report the on-time completion rate and the average days late.
testing.done: timeliness is recomputed against regulator-accepted dates with the on-time rate, late count and average days late reported.

testing.step: Test the sweep for the same defect elsewhere
actions: For three sampled findings, run the examiner's own test in two states or channels the exam did not cover.
Compare your result to the recorded sweep conclusion and flag any defect present that the sweep declared clean.
Confirm that where a sweep found contamination, the action scope and restitution population were actually extended.
Record the sweep re-performance evidence in the workpaper.
testing.done: sweep conclusions are re-performed in uncovered states or channels with any missed contamination logged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception recording the state, exam, finding id, the defect and the regulatory exposure it creates.

Assign a root cause (finding not decomposed, symptom-level action, date re-baselined without approval, closure on assertion, scope limited to the exam state, restitution population understated) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a closure is reversed, notify the regulator through the exam coordinator with counsel-cleared wording.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue reference, root cause, owner, remediation date, regulator notification decision and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-time completion rate, the closure-validation failure rate, restitution completeness and the count of repeat findings.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with workpaper references behind each figure.
Sign the validation conclusion personally for every consent-order finding, independent of the Compliance function that performed the remediation.
Report the result, any reversed closure and every repeat finding to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the on-time rate, validation failure rate, restitution completeness, repeat findings, conclusion and Board reporting date.
